releases.title: Shared library forms fill the right boxes
releases.summary: Every shared form in the Template Studio library now has clear field labels, fills only from the records each box belongs to, and carries the title printed on the form itself.

highlights.title: Readable fields
highlights.description: Boxes the PDFs called Text3 or undefined now say what goes in them, such as Landlord name or Seller ZIP code, and no two fields share a label.

highlights.title: No more client details in the wrong box
highlights.description: Address, phone and email boxes for a landlord, witness, seller or attorney no longer fill with the client's details. Captions fill from parties, case number and judge.

highlights.title: Wills and directives fill from the client
highlights.description: The testator, declarant or principal on wills, living wills and powers of attorney fills from the client. Agents, witnesses and notaries stay for you to type.

highlights.title: Correct titles and choices
highlights.description: Forms show their printed titles, such as ND Divorce With Children Summons or Ohio Request for Service, and radio choices read as the page prints them.

highlights.title: Probate guidebook fixes
highlights.description: The ND informal probate guidebook no longer puts names or email in County of and State of boxes, and places the decedent's domicile county and state correctly.

releases.title: Clearer Microsoft 365 and Google connections
releases.summary: Cloud setup now shows what each connection asks for and whose account it uses, names permissions that were not granted, and confirms each connect. Everyone can check and reconnect their own account from Profile.

highlights.title: Connect with a clear picture
highlights.description: Administration, Integrations, Cloud now lists what Microsoft 365 or Google will be asked to allow and who must sign in. A suite your firm does not use stays out of the way.

highlights.title: See and fix missing permissions
highlights.description: Declined permissions are named, the features they turn off are marked, and Re-authorize comes first. Personal Gmail firms can re-authorize; admins can disconnect.

highlights.title: Your own connected accounts
highlights.description: Profile, Connected accounts shows whether your own Microsoft 365 or Google account is connected, what that consent allows, and lets you connect or reconnect it.

highlights.title: Microsoft account type and Teams
highlights.description: Reconnecting Microsoft 365 now records the account type and who granted it. Teams no longer offers a reconnect that cannot help a personal Microsoft account.

releases.title: Guides with screenshots and step-by-step help
releases.summary: The user and administrator guides now walk through each screen step by step, with annotated screenshots and troubleshooting, and the Guide button opens the section for the screen you are on.

highlights.title: Screenshots with numbered steps
highlights.description: Key screens appear in the guides with numbered markers that match each step, from matters and tasks to invoices, Template Studio, and Administration.

highlights.title: Guide opens the right section
highlights.description: The Guide button opens the exact section for the screen or matter tab you are on, and each chapter's Open in LawHand buttons take you back.

highlights.title: Help inside panels
highlights.description: The Email tasks, e-signature, client paperwork, and expenses panels link straight to the guide section that explains them.

highlights.title: Troubleshooting in every chapter
highlights.description: Each chapter ends with common problems, their likely cause, and what to do, and the guides now match the current Template Studio test and publish steps.

highlights.title: Clearer forms and headings
highlights.description: Conflict Search and invoice fixed-fee fields show their borders again, and the Integrations overview heading is readable.

releases.title: Clearer recovery for matter storage
releases.summary: Missing matter folders now have a direct setup path and clearer retry guidance. Admin storage status distinguishes a saved provider preference and available connection from matter folder access, while Directory Sync remains separate.

highlights.title: Find a missing matter folder
highlights.description: A missing OneDrive or Google Drive matter folder means no file was stored. Use the matter's Document tools; check Administration, Integrations, then Cloud for connection issues.

highlights.title: Set up a folder, then retry
highlights.description: Use the single Set up folders action and wait for its status before retrying the save. Sync folder remains for a folder that is already provisioned.

highlights.title: Separate provider status from folder access
highlights.description: Preference saved confirms provider choice, not matter folder access. Connection status does not verify each folder; Directory Sync is separate and may depend on account tier.

releases.title: Run several assistant chats and queue follow-ups
releases.summary: The assistant can answer in several conversations at once and lets you queue your next question while it works. Review tags are easier to read, and the chat makes better use of a phone screen.

highlights.title: Keep several chats going
highlights.description: Up to three conversations can answer at the same time. The conversation list shows which are responding, which have a new reply and which need a look.

highlights.title: Queue your next question
highlights.description: Keep typing while an answer streams. What you send waits in a queue and goes out in order as each answer finishes; edit or remove it before then.

highlights.title: Nothing builds on a failed answer
highlights.description: If an answer fails, anything queued behind it is held until you choose to resume, so a follow-up never builds on a reply you did not see.

highlights.title: Review tags you can read
highlights.description: Cited, verify and model tags use stronger colors and explain themselves on hover. The full key opens from the chat header instead of covering your answers.

highlights.title: More room on a phone
highlights.description: Matter context sits under the conversation title, answers no longer pull you down while you read back, and Return starts a new line on touch keyboards.

highlights.title: Drafts stay with their conversation
highlights.description: A half-typed question stays in the conversation you typed it in when you switch to another one and back.

releases.title: Find and review firm and global templates
releases.summary: Search firm and global forms from a matter, preview shared sources and bring a reviewed copy into your firm. The new draft keeps its matter context and stays unavailable until tested and published.

highlights.title: Search firm and global forms
highlights.description: Search both catalogs by title and form details, then filter results to your firm's templates or the shared global library.

highlights.title: See which forms are ready to use
highlights.description: Published firm forms show their available version. Draft and paused forms are labeled and open in Studio for review.

highlights.title: Bring a global form into your firm
highlights.description: Preview the read-only source, then add it as a firm draft. The PDF and suggested fields enter the usual review flow with matter context; test and publish before use.

releases.title: PDF previews update as you work
releases.summary: Preparing a published PDF now fills available matter values and updates the preview automatically. Finish the missing answers, review the document and choose Save to matter.

highlights.title: See your answers without another click
highlights.description: The matter dialog and single-document Prepare page refresh PDF previews after a short pause in typing, including Word templates generated as PDFs.

highlights.title: Keep your place while reviewing
highlights.description: Page and zoom choices stay in place as the preview updates. An older preview is clearly marked while your latest answers are being rendered.

highlights.title: Save when the document is ready
highlights.description: Save to matter waits for required answers and an up-to-date preview. If previewing fails, a Retry preview action keeps your answers available.

releases.title: Find matters that need attention
releases.summary: Open the attention list from My Matters, clear personal filters together, and see when the loaded list covers only part of your assigned matters.

highlights.title: Open the attention list in one click
highlights.description: The attention heading opens the matching loaded matters, clearing conflicting personal filters while keeping your sort and other list choices.

highlights.title: Understand the list you are viewing
highlights.description: Partial lists show loaded and assigned counts. Attention labels describe their scope, and failed requests offer a retry instead of an empty list.

highlights.title: Clear filters together
highlights.description: Clear filter removes the personal keyword, status and attention filters in one action. Removing only the attention chip keeps your other filters.

releases.title: Reliable packet saves and clearer form review
releases.summary: Packet saves keep each document's result when you return. Form review distinguishes required answers and optional blanks, and Cloud Search can target a source and filename.

highlights.title: See which answers are required
highlights.description: Sample-fill counts update as you type. Required and optional filters separate unanswered questions, and unlabelled source fields explain when to check the PDF.

highlights.title: Review each suggested answer once
highlights.description: Verifying an answer clears its review step and survives reopening a packet. Changing the answer or unchecking verification requires a fresh review.

highlights.title: Search the source you intended
highlights.description: Choose OneDrive, Google Drive, SharePoint or email sources when testing cloud search. Exact phrase matching keeps a filename from becoming unrelated common-word results.

highlights.title: Find the right recovery step
highlights.description: Document folder errors point to the matter's Document tools and explain when to check the cloud connection. Failed saves clearly say no file was stored.

highlights.title: Keep packet save results
highlights.description: One save action records each document's result and can continue after you leave. Reopening shows saved files; retries keep recorded successes.

releases.title: Clear calendar results and safer shortcuts
releases.summary: Calendar list headings show the full displayed range. New event messages distinguish saving in LawHand, calendar synchronization and Zoom meeting creation.

highlights.title: Know which dates you are viewing
highlights.description: The calendar list names its complete date range, including when it crosses into another year.

highlights.title: Understand what saved
highlights.description: New event messages separate local saves, calendar updates and Zoom meetings. A Zoom failure preserves a successful calendar update.

highlights.title: Keep typing and confirming safely
highlights.description: The new-conversation shortcut stays inactive while you edit text, compose input or use a confirmation dialog.

releases.title: Visible PDF previews and simpler reconnection
releases.summary: Sample and packet PDFs open inside LawHand for review. Personal Microsoft and Google connections return you to Calendar with a clear result.

highlights.title: Return to your calendar
highlights.description: Connecting your own account brings you back to Calendar, including when you cancel or need to retry. You do not need administrator access.

highlights.title: Find the reconnect control
highlights.description: Open Calendar and choose Connect Calendar to reconnect your own account. Cloud status and help instructions now use that same path.

highlights.title: See the preview you requested
highlights.description: Sample and packet PDF previews open in a page viewer with zoom and page controls. Source loading and errors are visible, and Word packet previews offer a clearly labeled download.

releases.title: Reliable document completion and cloud tools
releases.summary: Saved documents close their drafts, packet dropdowns show usable suggestions, and printed-form reading has clearer progress. Microsoft search and the profile page are more reliable.

highlights.title: Let form reading finish
highlights.description: Longer printed-form reads no longer stop after 25 seconds in the browser. Keep the page open while it reads, then review the proposed details before accepting them.

highlights.title: Microsoft search requests repaired
highlights.description: File and mail searches use separate supported requests and respect the sources you selected.

highlights.title: Profile stays available
highlights.description: Time-entry totals no longer stop the profile page from opening.

highlights.title: Close a draft after saving
highlights.description: A saved document leaves your in-progress list. If closing the draft needs a retry, the saved document is kept and the retry does not create another copy.

highlights.title: Usable packet choices
highlights.description: State abbreviations match available options; unmatched suggestions stay missing. The intake sample no longer prints formatting marks around its questions.

releases.title: Fill from a matter and keep your progress
releases.summary: Sample forms can use existing matter details, with a PDF preview beside the answers. Preparing documents also gets more reliable draft recovery, complete packet questions, and clearer cloud connection status.

highlights.title: Start with the matter
highlights.description: Search by client, matter name or number to fill a sample from existing details. Review missing answers and preview the filled PDF before downloading.

highlights.title: Reliable drafts and packets
highlights.description: Prepare restores answers and verified fields before refreshing matter data. Packets include Markdown questions, choice controls and a preview of each document.

highlights.title: Clearer forms and connection status
highlights.description: Intake choices keep their question text. Fee-agreement labels identify each signer, source defaults are visible, and storage status shows connections needing attention.

releases.title: Search inside a matter's documents
releases.summary: The Documents tab's search box now looks inside the documents' text, scans included, and the assistant can pull matching excerpts into a matter's context. Also two small hardening changes to workflow document requests.

highlights.title: Found inside documents
highlights.description: Type three or more characters in the Documents search and excerpts from the documents' text appear beneath the toolbar, each with an Open link. Scans read by OCR are included.

highlights.title: Excerpts for the assistant
highlights.description: The matter context tool gains an excerpts section: give it a question and it returns the matching passages from the matter's documents, fenced as untrusted text.

highlights.title: Workflow documents hardened
highlights.description: Document requests on an approved workflow version are now immutable at the database, like its stages, and a saved-document rollback blocker is labelled as a document step.

releases.title: Workflows can ask for documents
releases.summary: A workflow template can list documents to prepare. When a run is approved, each one is pre-filled from the matter by Smart Fill and handed to its assignee as a Prepare task. A person still reviews, verifies and saves it.

highlights.title: Documents on a workflow template
highlights.description: Under Workflow settings, add published document templates beside the checklist, with a stage, a due offset and an assignee role. The preview says if one cannot be prepared.

highlights.title: Pre-filled and handed over
highlights.description: Approving the run opens a Smart Fill session per document, filled from the matter, and a Prepare task linking to it. The assignee resumes it from Documents in progress.

highlights.title: Rollback keeps saved work
highlights.description: Rolling a run back cancels the Prepare tasks and discards unsaved sessions. A document already saved from its session blocks the rollback rather than being removed.

releases.title: Resume a packet, and save it in the background
releases.summary: What you type on the Prepare page is kept for 14 days and can be resumed from the matter's Documents tab. A previewed packet can be saved in the background, and the ready-to-review banner shows how many fields you verified.

highlights.title: Pick up where you left off
highlights.description: Answers and verified ticks are kept server-side, encrypted, for 14 days. The matter's Documents tab lists documents in progress with Resume and Discard.

highlights.title: Save all in the background
highlights.description: Once every document in a packet is previewed, queue the saves on the server and leave the page. Each document reports Saved or why not; an expired preview asks for a new one.

highlights.title: Verified counts on the banner
highlights.description: The ready-to-review banner on Case Documents now shows how many fields you verified for each document.

releases.title: Template sets: one interview, a whole packet
releases.summary: Group the templates you file together into a set, answer the shared questions once, preview every document, save them all to the matter one after another, and send the signable ones, all from the Prepare page.

highlights.title: Sets in Template Studio
highlights.description: Name a set, choose published templates in the order they are produced, and pin a version where a filed packet needs one. Prepare on a matter starts the packet from there.

highlights.title: Asked once, filled everywhere
highlights.description: A question bound to the same record in several documents is asked once and says how many documents it fills. Smart Fill answers it from the matter.

highlights.title: Preview, save and send the packet
highlights.description: Generate all previews (a failed one retries alone), save all to the matter one document at a time with each result shown, then send each signable PDF from the same page.

releases.title: Fill from the matter's documents, and AI for unreadable handwriting
releases.summary: A blank template field can now be filled from what the matter's documents say, marked for review with the source one click away. When a hand-filled form has fields OCR cannot read, an opt-in AI read can try each clip.

highlights.title: Documents as a fill source
highlights.description: Values read from the matter's documents fill fields nothing else filled. They never replace a matter or client value, are marked for review, and link to the document.

highlights.title: A new scan refreshes readiness
highlights.description: When an uploaded document yields values, the matter's ready-to-review documents are recomputed, so the Case Documents banner reflects the scan.

highlights.title: AI for unreadable handwriting, opt-in
highlights.description: Reading a printed form against its template can send only the clips OCR could not read to the AI provider, one metered call each, when the firm allows it.

releases.title: Verify filled fields quickly, and read scanned or hand-filled forms
releases.summary: Tick or press Enter to verify each filled field before saving, and the names travel with the document. Matter documents can now be read by OCR, and a printed, hand-filled form is read field by field against the template that printed it.

highlights.title: Click through and verify
highlights.description: Each filled field has a Verified tick. Press Enter to verify and move to the next. Typing a value counts as checking it. Optional, never a gate; the Documents tab shows the count.

highlights.title: Scans and photos are read too
highlights.description: Find details now reads a scanned PDF or an image through OCR when there is no text layer, and shows how sure the reader was for each value. Re-reading the same file is instant.

highlights.title: Read a hand-filled form against its template
highlights.description: A scan of a form the matter printed can be read field by field against that form, with a clip of the handwriting beside each value. Nothing is saved until you accept it.

releases.title: Send for signature right after you prepare a document
releases.summary: A PDF prepared from a template with signature fields now offers Send for signature on the same page, with the matter's client filled in as the signer and the same checks the matter's E-Signature panel applies.

highlights.title: A Send step after Save
highlights.description: When the saved PDF has signature fields, the Prepare page stays open with signers, dates and reminders ready. The client's name and email come from the matter.

highlights.title: One form, wherever you send from
highlights.description: The matter's E-Signature panel and the Prepare page use the same request form, so placement review, role checks and the signing-plan acknowledgement behave the same.

highlights.title: Word templates with signature fields default to PDF
highlights.description: Only a PDF can be sent for signature, so a Word template with signature fields is generated as PDF unless you choose the editable Word document, and the page says why.

releases.title: Prepare a document from Studio, straight into the matter
releases.summary: A published template can be taken from Template Studio to a matter in one guided page: choose the matter, review the filled fields and the exact preview, and save it into that matter's documents.

highlights.title: Use on a matter, from Studio
highlights.description: A published template in Studio has a Use on a matter button. It opens a guided page: Template, Matter, Populate, Review, Save. A draft says to publish a tested version first.

highlights.title: Same review, wherever you start
highlights.description: The page is the Generate dialog's own fill and preview logic, so a document prepared here is reviewed under exactly the same rules before it is saved.

highlights.title: Lands on the matter with the document open
highlights.description: Saving takes you to the matter's Case Documents with the new document's preview open. Ready-to-review documents and the probate packet open the same page with the matter chosen.

releases.title: Documents are prepared the moment a matter has data
releases.summary: When a matter is created, converted from a lead, or receives intake answers, LawHand fills every published template from it in the background and the matter page shows what is ready to review.

highlights.title: Ready to review, without a click
highlights.description: Case Documents shows how many published templates fill from this matter and how much of each is filled, with what still needs a person. Open one and it is already filled in.

highlights.title: Nothing is generated or sent on its own
highlights.description: The background run records counts and field names only. Reviewing, previewing and saving a document stay yours, and sending for signature is a separate step.

highlights.title: Refreshes as the matter grows
highlights.description: A questionnaire coming back or accepted intake updates queue a fresh run. If details changed since the last run, the panel says so; opening a document always fills from live data.

highlights.title: Converted leads count as new matters
highlights.description: Opening a matter from a lead now fires the same matter-created trigger as creating one directly, so firm workflow rules and document preparation both see it.

releases.title: Smart Fill reaches more of the matter and fills the right way
releases.summary: Document fill reads the client's name parts, the matter number and opening date, and every party role, fits each value to its field, and is proven against mock and real forms before it reaches a page.

highlights.title: Letters can open with a first name
highlights.description: Fields named first_name or last_name, or bound to the client's name parts, organization or client number, fill from the contact record. Name matches are offered for review.

highlights.title: Every party role fills its caption
highlights.description: Petitioner, respondent, opposing party, counsel, witness and expert rows fill their own fields, as plaintiff and defendant always did. A family caption no longer stays blank.

highlights.title: Values fit their fields
highlights.description: A state code selects a court form's dropdown option, a yes checks a box, a date field reads MM/DD/YYYY. A value a field cannot hold is left for you rather than forced in.

highlights.title: Matter number and date opened
highlights.description: The matter's number, practice area and opening date are available to templates by name or binding.

highlights.title: The estate fills by field name
highlights.description: A probate form field named after an estate value fills with or without a binding; before, it reported as filled and rendered blank.

releases.title: Assistant drafts keep their formatting, and can update tasks
releases.summary: Documents drafted in ChatGPT, Claude, or Codex now arrive in LawHand with their headings, emphasis, and lists intact, and a connected assistant can propose a task update for a person to approve.

highlights.title: Draft formatting survives the push
highlights.description: Headings, bold and italic text, bullet and numbered lists, quotes, code, and tables from an external assistant arrive in the matter as real Word formatting.

highlights.title: Task updates, still approved by a person
highlights.description: A connected assistant can propose a status, assignee, priority, due-date, or note change on a task; a reviewer approves it before LawHand applies it.

highlights.title: Clearer limits when a draft is too big
highlights.description: If a pushed document or citation list is over the limit, the error now names the submitted size and the allowed limit instead of a generic rejection.

releases.title: North Dakota probate: intake picks the proceeding, forms pre-fill
releases.summary: A plain-language probate intake, answered in the portal, on paper, or by phone, works out which North Dakota proceeding an estate needs and fills the court's informal-probate forms from the estate record for attorney review.

highlights.title: One intake, three ways to answer it
highlights.description: Clients answer in the portal with date, yes/no and money controls, save and come back later, mark what they don't know, fill in the paper form, or read it to the office by phone.

highlights.title: The proceeding, with the statute
highlights.description: The Probate tab names the track and says why, citing N.D.C.C. Title 30.1, and lists the NDPC forms to file with the pages to print. Correct a fact to change the answer.

highlights.title: Court forms pre-loaded and pre-filled
highlights.description: The court's informal-probate packet ships with LawHand, installs into your templates on first use, and fills from the estate record for review before anything is generated.

highlights.title: The probate clock
highlights.description: Enter the appointment and publication dates and the statutory deadlines appear on the estate and, if you choose, as matter tasks.

highlights.title: Clients list what the estate owns
highlights.description: After appointment, the client portal shows an Estate inventory tab. Items wait for staff to verify before they count toward the inventory.

releases.title: Word templates place their signature fields themselves
releases.summary: Word templates now place their signature fields on the generated PDF by the caption printed beside each one, so a document made from Word is ready to send like one made from a PDF template.

highlights.title: Word templates place their own signature fields
highlights.description: A signing field in a Word template is placed at its caption in the generated PDF, so no one has to position it by hand.

highlights.title: The caption is read from the document, or set in Studio
highlights.description: The text around the field in the Word document is the default; a Word signing field in Template Studio can name a different caption.

highlights.title: Signature lines print as rules
highlights.description: A signing field in a generated Word document now prints as a ruled line for the signer instead of a blank gap.

releases.title: Email LawHand to route tasks, reviews, and deadlines
releases.summary: Staff can save one LawHand Tasks contact and send firm-wide or matter-specific work with consistent TASK, REVIEW, and DEADLINE subjects. Every request remains reviewable before it becomes matter work.

highlights.title: One vocabulary wherever you send
highlights.description: TASK, REVIEW, and DEADLINE subjects behave consistently on the firm address and each matter address, including a required confirmed date for deadlines.

highlights.title: Firm email work lives with Tasks
highlights.description: The saved firm contact and Needs review queue now live on Tasks, where staff choose the matter, owner, title, and date before filing.

highlights.title: Normal task follow-through
highlights.description: Reviewed firm email work now uses the same assignment notice and connected-calendar projection as other LawHand tasks after the task is safely created.

releases.title: Signature requests are checked before they are sent
releases.summary: Before a signature request goes to a client, staff see where each signer will sign. A plan the system had to guess at is held until someone confirms it.

highlights.title: See where each signer will sign before sending
highlights.description: Preparing a request now shows every signer's fields by page, with where each came from, before anything reaches the client.

highlights.title: A guessed plan waits for a look
highlights.description: When no signature line was found for a signer, or too many were, sending is held until staff confirm they have checked it.

highlights.title: Case Setup puts the same warning on the timeline
highlights.description: Intake sends without a staff step, so a guessed signing plan is recorded on the matter timeline for the firm to see.

releases.title: A document that cannot be signed now tells you why
releases.summary: A document generated from a template that has no signing positions now names the field that is wrong and what to change. Templates whose signing fields could never bind are refused at publish.

highlights.title: The blocked document names the field
highlights.description: Sending for signature used to ask only for a position review. It now names the signing field that did not bind and the change that clears it.

highlights.title: One bad field no longer discards the good ones
highlights.description: A single misconfigured signing field used to throw away every other placement in the template. Only the broken one is reported now.

highlights.title: Word documents say to regenerate as PDF
highlights.description: Signing positions can only be placed on a PDF, so a Word document that needs them now points to Word-to-PDF conversion instead.

highlights.title: Unsignable templates are caught at publish
highlights.description: A template whose signature fields have no signer role, or were never positioned, is refused with those fields named.

highlights.title: Signature lines on outside paperwork are read correctly
highlights.description: Lines captioned "Client:", "By:", "MOTHER" or "Plaintiff", dates printed left or above, and fill-in blanks are now told apart, so nobody signs another party's line.

releases.title: Your cloud folders stay yours through staff changes
releases.summary: Google Workspace onboarding now stores the matter root in an organisation-owned Shared Drive, so documents stay with the firm when an administrator leaves. LawHand shows who owns the root and never deletes customer cloud folders.

highlights.title: Your documents stay with the firm
highlights.description: On Google Workspace, LawHand creates an organisation-owned Shared Drive and keeps the matter root inside it, so access survives the administrator who connected leaving.

highlights.title: Nothing is deleted when you leave
highlights.description: Your folders live in your own cloud account. LawHand never deletes or renames them on disconnect, matter close, or when your firm leaves.

highlights.title: Personal accounts are labelled honestly
highlights.description: A personal Google root sits in one person's Drive, so onboarding reports it as at risk instead of claiming organisation ownership.

releases.title: Cloud setup stays accurate when you revisit it
releases.summary: Administrators can revisit every onboarding step without being sent back to the completed screen, and an existing Personal Google connection is identified correctly throughout setup.

highlights.title: Review remains reachable
highlights.description: Restarting setup now keeps the full wizard open through Review, including after a browser refresh, while the existing workspace and cloud root remain live.

highlights.title: Personal Google stays personal
highlights.description: A connected Gmail or Google One account is labeled Personal Google and describes Gmail, Drive, and Calendar access without implying Workspace directory sync.

releases.title: Cloud storage setup carries the LawHand name
releases.summary: Cloud onboarding now names the actual lawhand-records folder. Google-only health and Personal Google reviews also accurately reflect the connected account without implying Workspace directory access.

highlights.title: The setup instructions match your cloud
highlights.description: The storage step now names lawhand-records before creation and confirms that same folder afterward. Existing legacy folders remain supported through the controlled migration path.

highlights.title: Google-only setup no longer looks broken
highlights.description: A healthy Google connection stays healthy when Microsoft 365 is not connected, and Personal Google no longer claims that a Workspace directory was synchronized or required.

releases.title: Onboarding tells the truth about setup and account access
releases.summary: Firms can defer setup without false completion evidence, cloud agreement gating follows the controlled rollout setting, and solo Google accounts can connect Gmail, Drive, and Calendar without pretending to sync a Workspace directory.

highlights.title: Set up later is honest
highlights.description: Deferring setup keeps your core workspace available and leaves onboarding ready to re-enter; it does not claim that integrations, storage, or team import are complete.

highlights.title: Choose the right Google account
highlights.description: Google Workspace administrators can enable directory sync, while Personal Google / Google One connects Gmail, Drive, and Calendar without requesting directory access.

highlights.title: Cloud setup is fail-closed
highlights.description: When agreement enforcement is enabled, new cloud connections wait for current agreements; controlled rollout remains visibly non-blocking.

releases.title: Scans and prose can be read too, when you ask
releases.summary: Document reading can now use a metered AI pass to find matter and client details a form field or label missed, such as a scan or a fact stated in a sentence. It is opt-in per firm and per document, and every value is yours to review.

highlights.title: For scans and prose
highlights.description: A PDF with no text layer, a form whose labels have drifted, or a detail written in a sentence can now be proposed instead of missed.

highlights.title: Only when you ask
highlights.description: The AI pass is off by default until your firm enables it, and on any document you tick the box to allow it for that read.

highlights.title: Still reviewed, never automatic
highlights.description: AI values arrive as proposals beside the deterministic ones. Nothing is written until you accept a value, and a value the document does not contain is refused.

releases.title: A filled intake form fills the matter for you
releases.summary: A filled intake form or fee agreement that lands on a matter can be read for the details it already contains. Each supported matter or client field is proposed for review, and nothing is saved until a person accepts it.

highlights.title: The answers you already have
highlights.description: Open a filled PDF form, or a document with clear “Label: value” lines, and LawHand proposes the matter and client details it can read.

highlights.title: Reviewed, then recorded against the matter
highlights.description: Accept a proposed value and it is written to the matter or client record with its source. A value the document no longer supports is refused.

highlights.title: Off until your firm switches it on
highlights.description: Reading documents at upload is opt-in per firm. Until then, the review panel is still available on any matter document you choose.

releases.title: Trial access starts only after approval
releases.summary: A firm can request access without starting a trial or AI spend; the LawHand team approves the workspace, controls its end date, and keeps expensive Premium AI under a separate switch.

highlights.title: Register, then wait for approval
highlights.description: A registration starts no trial clock and grants no workspace access. LawHand emails the firm after an operator approves its bounded trial.

highlights.title: An extension arrives by email
highlights.description: When the LawHand team extends a trial, firm administrators receive a branded email with the new end date.

highlights.title: Premium AI stays a deliberate exception
highlights.description: A trial extension does not turn on Premium AI. If LawHand sponsors it for a trial, that grant is explicit and can be withdrawn separately.

releases.title: One place to lay out a form, not two
releases.summary: Uploading a form now scans it and hands you straight to the template editor, instead of asking you to lay the fields out twice in two screens that had quietly drifted apart.

highlights.title: Upload, then edit — in one editor
highlights.description: The upload step scans your document and shows what it found; laying out and naming the fields happens in the template editor, where you can also test, version and publish.

highlights.title: A scan that found nothing is no longer a dead end
highlights.description: A flat PDF with no detectable fields can be saved as a draft, so you can open it in the editor and place the fields yourself.

highlights.title: The editor shows what needs checking
highlights.description: Fields are coloured by whether they were read confidently, taken from the document's own form controls, or placed by hand — with an AI proposal marked as one.

highlights.title: A page that will not display no longer hides it
highlights.description: Where the document cannot be shown, the editor offers the original file and stops you placing a field whose position it cannot work out.

releases.title: A scanned form cannot be published unchecked
releases.summary: Where a scan was unsure of a field, someone now has to compare it with the original document before the template can be published — and they do it on the screen where they can fix what they find.

highlights.title: The source check is now enforced, not just asked for
highlights.description: A PDF or image template with fields the scan was unsure of cannot be published until someone confirms they compared them with the original document.

highlights.title: Check the form where you can correct it
highlights.description: The confirmation moved from the upload step to the template editor, so a field that looks wrong can be fixed on the spot instead of only ticked off.

highlights.title: Changing the fields asks again
highlights.description: Adding, removing or moving a field withdraws the confirmation, because it no longer describes the form that was checked.

highlights.title: A clean scan asks for nothing
highlights.description: Where every field came straight from the document's own form fields, there is nothing uncertain to confirm and no extra step.

releases.title: Say what fills a form field, and see how much of it fills
releases.summary: The upload flow can now say where each field's value comes from, and both editors report how many of a form's fields fill themselves from the matter instead of being retyped.

highlights.title: Choose a data source while you review an uploaded form
highlights.description: The Fills from control is now on the screen where a form's fields are first reviewed, for PDF and Word uploads alike, rather than only in Template Studio later.

highlights.title: See how much of a form fills itself
highlights.description: Every editor reports how many fields arrive filled from the matter, broken down into bound, filled by field name, typed by hand, signed and no source.

highlights.title: Colour the page by where each value comes from
highlights.description: A Fill source highlight recolours the fields on the document so a wired part of a form is distinguishable at a glance from a wall of retyping.

highlights.title: A warning before a rename quietly breaks a fill
highlights.description: A field filling only because its name matches a known record now says so, and says that renaming it stops the fill, which nothing previously told anyone.

highlights.title: Publishing a card-bound template is no longer refused
highlights.description: A required field bound with the card picker was refused at publish for having no data source, although it filled correctly. Approval now resolves it the same way the fill does.

releases.title: Paying ends your trial, and billing stays reachable
releases.summary: Subscribing during a free trial now ends the trial straight away, a trial that has run out can still reach billing to pay, and premium AI becomes available once a firm subscribes.

highlights.title: Paying ends the trial at once
highlights.description: Subscribing during your free trial clears the trial end date, so your firm keeps working past the day the trial would have ended.

highlights.title: You can always reach billing to pay
highlights.description: If a trial runs out, an administrator can still sign in and open Billing to subscribe. Other pages wait until the subscription is active.

highlights.title: One trial, not two
highlights.description: Subscribing no longer starts a second free period at the payment provider, so the first charge arrives when you expect it.

highlights.title: Premium AI turns on when you subscribe
highlights.description: Premium AI stays off during a trial across chat, plugins, templates, document drafting and email drafts, and is available once the firm subscribes.

releases.title: Invitations work, and sign-in explains a refusal
releases.summary: Invited colleagues can accept by choosing a password or continuing with Google or Microsoft, and a refused Google or Microsoft sign-in now explains why instead of showing an error code.

highlights.title: Accept an invitation your way
highlights.description: The invitation email opens a page for your firm where you set a password or continue with the Google or Microsoft account the invitation was sent to.

highlights.title: Invitations are single use and expire
highlights.description: Each link works once and expires after seven days. Administrators can resend or revoke an invitation from the Users list, where invited people now appear.

highlights.title: A clear message when sign-in is refused
highlights.description: If Google or Microsoft sign-in cannot continue, for example for an account that has not been invited, the sign-in page says why and what to do next.

highlights.title: Earlier invitation links still open
highlights.description: Invitations sent before this update open the new page and get a fresh seven-day window.

releases.title: Assistant settings stick, and document access says who can see what
releases.summary: Reopening an assistant conversation keeps the response settings you chose, the client portal explains what the client can actually open, and the sample form library tells same-titled forms apart.

highlights.title: Your assistant settings survive a reopen
highlights.description: The response model and the public case law choice are saved on the conversation, so closing and reopening it no longer resets them to the defaults.

highlights.title: Firm case law policy is respected and explained
highlights.description: Turning off public case law in Settings now applies to the assistant. The chat switch shows it off and says the firm restricts it, rather than looking available.

highlights.title: One answer to what the client can see
highlights.description: The portal's document count matches its Documents tab, and shows what makes up the total: shared by your firm, available for signing, and sent by the client.

highlights.title: Signing paperwork is no longer labelled Private
highlights.description: A document a client can open because they are signing it now reads Available to signing client on the matter documents tab, with the share toggle unchanged.

highlights.title: Sample forms that share a title are told apart
highlights.description: Where several library forms carry the same title, each is numbered with its field count and, where the source recorded one, its edition, with a note to preview first.

releases.title: Starter forms generate again, and fill from more of the client record
releases.summary: The three forms every firm starts with can produce a document again, an optional checkbox stays optional, and templates can pull more of what the client already told you.

highlights.title: The starter forms produce documents again
highlights.description: Every checkbox on the fee agreement, client questionnaire and intake form was marked required, so none could be generated. They work with any combination of answers now.

highlights.title: An optional checkbox stays optional
highlights.description: Marking a checkbox optional in the field editor now holds when you save. Where a requirement cannot be lifted, the editor says so instead of turning itself back on.

highlights.title: More of the client record fills itself
highlights.description: A template field can now draw a client's date of birth, second phone, preferred contact method and time, language, referral source, and emergency contact details.

highlights.title: A name box is no longer treated as a place to initial
highlights.description: A field labelled with Middle Initial was read as a signing box and asked the client to initial inside their own name. It stays an ordinary field.

highlights.title: Uploaded forms show their fields in review
highlights.description: A page preview of a fillable PDF came back with the printed text and blank space where the boxes should be. The boxes are drawn.

releases.title: Existing engagements, open dates, and bulk matter creation
releases.summary: Open a matter that is already engaged without sending paperwork, set the date it was really opened, and create many matters and clients at once from a CSV template.

highlights.title: Record an existing engagement
highlights.description: Open a matter as already engaged: file the signed fee agreement, note it was signed with no copy on hand, or record that there is no agreement and why. Nothing is sent.

highlights.title: Add the signed copy later
highlights.description: A matter recorded without its signed agreement offers Add signed copy on its paperwork card; the matters list badges and filters these engagements.

highlights.title: Open date
highlights.description: New matters take the date the firm actually opened them. Lists and the matter page show it, and it can be corrected from the matter details.

highlights.title: Bulk create from CSV
highlights.description: Download a template, fill one row per matter, review how each client and attorney resolves, and create the matters and any new clients together.

releases.title: Clearer matter actions, real deadline times, stronger evidence
releases.summary: "Active" means one thing on My Matters, the View link opens the matter, task due times reach Outlook and Google at the hour you set, an unfilable signed copy raises a task, and certificates record the signer's address.

highlights.title: "Active" has one meaning
highlights.description: The My Matters row control is now "Work on this" / "Working on this". It marks you as working the matter and never changes the matter's status.

highlights.title: The View link opens the matter
highlights.description: The View arrow on a matter row is a real link and reachable by keyboard. It previously looked clickable and did nothing.

highlights.title: Deadlines keep their time on your calendar
highlights.description: A task with a due time reaches Outlook and Google as a timed event instead of an all-day entry, and the synced copy no longer appears beside the task.

highlights.title: An unfilable signed copy raises a task
highlights.description: When filing a signed document keeps failing, an assigned follow-up task is raised on the matter. Filing keeps retrying and the task closes when it succeeds.

highlights.title: Certificates record the signer's address
highlights.description: A signing evidence certificate records the signer's own address rather than an internal one of ours, and says so plainly when none can be attributed.

releases.title: Drag a task on the calendar
releases.summary: Drag an open task deadline to a new day or hour and choose what the drop means: move the due date, or block working time for it.

highlights.title: Move a due date by dragging it
highlights.description: Drop a task deadline on another day, or on an hour in Day and Week view to set its time. Its reminder is re-armed for the new date and its Outlook or Google copy follows.

highlights.title: Block time to work on something
highlights.description: Choose Block time instead and the calendar gets a work block linked to the task, while the due date and its reminders stay exactly where they were.

releases.title: Cleaner signing fields and matter details
releases.summary: Signature lines are offered only where a client signs, court and judge can be edited, closed matters no longer offer paperwork, and a voided invoice shows no balance.

highlights.title: Only real signature lines
highlights.description: Firm-use lines such as Referred by and Reviewed by are no longer offered as fields for the client to sign.

highlights.title: Court and judge are editable
highlights.description: Add or correct a matter's court and judge from the matter's details and the new-matter form.

highlights.title: Closed matters do not offer paperwork
highlights.description: A closed matter shows why sending client paperwork is unavailable instead of offering an action that cannot run.

highlights.title: Voided invoices show no balance
highlights.description: Voiding an invoice clears the balance staff see while keeping the invoice record and its total.

releases.title: Straighter answers about tasks and deadlines
releases.summary: Ask administrative questions without being turned away, see every open task, and push deadlines that keep their time and do not double up.

highlights.title: Administrative questions get answered
highlights.description: Asking who is assigned no longer returns a research notice. Questions that do ask for a legal conclusion are still held to cited authority.

highlights.title: Every open task, and deadlines that stay put
highlights.description: The assistant sees all open tasks on a matter. Deadlines pushed to Outlook or Google keep your time zone and are not created twice.

releases.title: Conflict results respect matter access
releases.summary: Conflict search results now hide matters you are not assigned to, and tell you when something was withheld.

highlights.title: Restricted matters stay restricted
highlights.description: A conflict search shows matter names only for matters you are on. Administrators still see everything.

highlights.title: Nothing is hidden silently
highlights.description: When a result withholds a matter, the response reports how many were withheld so a reviewer knows to escalate.

releases.title: Conflict searches catch more of the same name
releases.summary: Find a person whose name you typed in a different order or with a middle name, and see opposing parties recorded only on the matter.

highlights.title: Type the name the way you have it
highlights.description: A search matches when the words of a name appear in any order, so "Smith, Alice" from a caption or a name entered with a middle name still finds the contact on file.

highlights.title: See opposing parties recorded on the matter
highlights.description: A matter whose counterparty matches your search is reported even when it also stores a client contact. Each matter is still listed once.

releases.title: Clearer matter checks and follow-ups
releases.summary: Find contacts by full name, see accurate deadline labels, and understand when an action needs a retry.

highlights.title: Find full names and keep follow-ups current
highlights.description: Conflict searches match a contact's combined first and last name. Once required paperwork is complete, its document-chasing task gives way to the scheduling follow-up.

highlights.title: See clearer dates and errors
highlights.description: Deadlines keep their calendar day. Save errors explain the failure and retry wait. A failed document load no longer looks like an empty folder.

releases.title: Keep AI connections working through updates
releases.summary: Existing AI routes keep their working connections, and the maintenance notice stays readable during updates.

highlights.title: Keep existing AI routes working
highlights.description: Saved AI connections retain their registered names until a replacement is activated. Your selected models and data permissions stay the same.

highlights.title: See the maintenance notice during updates
highlights.description: The maintenance page remains readable while application services restart, avoiding a permission error in place of the notice.

releases.title: Reliable signed files and matter numbering
releases.summary: Signed paperwork can finish filing, and simultaneous first matters keep a consistent firm number prefix.

highlights.title: Keep completed forms with the matter
highlights.description: Filing retries reuse the saved answers and signatures. Once filed, clients can download the completed forms and their evidence certificates from Documents.

highlights.title: Keep your matter numbers consistent
highlights.description: When the first matters are opened at the same time, they use the same firm prefix and receive separate consecutive numbers.

releases.title: Setup chooses document storage, and integrations show health first
releases.summary: New firms confirm where matter documents live during setup, and the Integrations page now leads with whether each connection works, with operator tools tucked under Advanced.

highlights.title: Choose where documents live during setup
highlights.description: The setup wizard has a Storage step: pick Google Drive or OneDrive from the accounts you connected, and LawHand creates the records folder and shows you where it is.

highlights.title: Re-authorizing a provider now shows that it worked
highlights.description: A successful re-authorization clears the old failure right away instead of leaving a stale reconnect warning beside a working connection.

highlights.title: Integrations answer "is this working?" at a glance
highlights.description: Each card shows a status pill, provider cards lead with the remedy when a connection cannot be used, and firm-wide and per-user connections are reported separately.

highlights.title: Storage settings and operator tools are out of the way
highlights.description: Changing the document provider asks for confirmation, and migration, import and readiness tools sit under Advanced for administrators who manage integrations.

releases.title: Reliable filing after clients sign
releases.summary: Signed forms can finish filing without waiting on their own cloud connection lock, and background retries keep each matter's tenant context.

highlights.title: Recover signed forms without signing again
highlights.description: Saved answers and signatures are reused when filing retries. Once filed, the signed PDF and evidence certificate are available in the client's Documents tab.

releases.title: Clearer legal team contact details
releases.summary: The client portal shows your legal team's names and email addresses without internal assignment labels.

highlights.title: Simple team contact details
highlights.description: Find your legal team's names and email links in the matter overview, without internal role codes beside their names.

releases.title: Flexible matter billing and Helcim subscriptions
releases.summary: Prepare invoices from selected work, one-time fees or agreed stages, and opt into recurring drafts while keeping control of sending and payment.

highlights.title: Bill the work and fees you choose
highlights.description: Choose invoice and work cutoff dates, add fixed fees without dummy time, and find older unbilled work in Ready to bill.

highlights.title: Track stages and prepare recurring drafts
highlights.description: Mark agreed stage fees ready and enable monthly or quarterly drafts for selected matters. Existing matters stay on their current billing workflow.

highlights.title: Offer dated installments
highlights.description: Record installments against one invoice and let clients see and pay them in the portal. Fixed-fee invoices use existing QuickBooks mappings after review.

highlights.title: Manage your LawHand subscription with Helcim
highlights.description: Review subscription pricing, securely add a card, update payment details and manage your LawHand plan. Your firm’s manual invoices and QuickBooks integration remain separate.

releases.title: Password reset emails that actually arrive
releases.summary: LawHand now sends its own account emails — password resets and address verification — through a dedicated mail service, from an address reserved for security messages.

highlights.title: Reset your password without waiting on email that never comes
highlights.description: Account emails are sent through a service built for them, so a reset link reaches your inbox instead of being filtered on the way.

highlights.title: Security email kept apart from everyday notifications
highlights.description: Password resets arrive from a separate address to task and document notifications, so filtering the everyday mail cannot hide the message you need to get back into your account.

highlights.title: Addresses that stop working are noticed
highlights.description: When an address permanently rejects mail, LawHand records it and stops sending there, instead of quietly retrying an inbox that no longer exists.

releases.title: Forward email into matter to-dos
releases.summary: Save one LawHand contact on your phone, forward a client email with [TASK], then confirm its matter, owner and optional date in Needs review.

highlights.title: One forwarding contact for your firm
highlights.description: Administrators can enable a firm address and staff can save the LawHand contact from Matters. Forward with [TASK] Jane, review this tomorrow.

highlights.title: Review the details and create a matter to-do
highlights.description: Confirm the suggested matter, colleague and date before creating work. The source email stays with the matter. User and admin guides explain setup and review.

releases.title: Draw your signature, place signing spots, and hear when clients sign
releases.summary: Clients can draw their signature, paperwork forms get the E-Signature panel's signing-spot placement, signed forms read as signed while filing, you get an email when the client signs, and requests go out from your mailbox.

highlights.title: Draw your signature in the portal
highlights.description: Clients can now draw their signature with a mouse, pen or finger as well as type their name. The drawing is stamped on the signed copy; the typed name stays on the record.

highlights.title: Place signing spots on paperwork forms
highlights.description: Send client paperwork now offers the same signing-position review as the E-Signature panel, so a PDF with no form fields still gets a clickable place to sign.

highlights.title: Signed forms read as signed while filing
highlights.description: When every signer has signed but the copy is still being filed to your storage, the client checklist and your paperwork strip say Signed, filing instead of asking again.

highlights.title: An email when the client signs
highlights.description: Whoever sent a document for signature gets an email the moment the last signer signs, before the copy is filed, so a storage problem cannot hide that the client acted.

highlights.title: Signature requests come from your mailbox
highlights.description: Invitations and reminders to sign now leave through the sending user's connected Google or Microsoft mailbox, as intake paperwork does, so your sent folder keeps the record.

highlights.title: Starter templates say what they need
highlights.description: The starter fee agreement and intake forms are drafts until an attorney tests and publishes them. They no longer show as ready, and using one says to publish it first.

releases.title: Rename your firm and edit its profile in one place
releases.summary: Administration has a Firm Profile tab. It renames the firm — including the name sign-up guessed from your email domain — and holds the contact details and branding that clients see on portal invitations, invoices and statements.

highlights.title: Fix the firm name sign-up guessed from your domain
highlights.description: Sign-up derived a firm name from your email domain and nothing could change it. Administration → Firm Profile now renames the firm everywhere clients see it.

highlights.title: Firm details moved out of the Settings tab
highlights.description: Firm name, contact details and branding were the fifth card inside Settings. They now have their own tab in Administration, next to Users.

releases.title: Answers keep running when you leave the chat
releases.summary: A long answer no longer disappears when you open another part of LawHand while it is being written. It keeps going, and it is there when you come back to the conversation.

highlights.title: Leave the chat without losing the answer
highlights.description: Opening matters, invoices or any other screen mid-answer used to cancel it. The answer now finishes and is saved to the conversation.

highlights.title: Pick the answer back up where it got to
highlights.description: Reopen the conversation while it is still being written and the answer carries on in front of you instead of showing only your question.

releases.title: Sessions that end when you end them
releases.summary: Resetting your password now signs out everyone using your account and disconnects your AI assistants, and the app tells you which ones to reconnect. Unused sessions sign out after 12 hours.

highlights.title: A password reset signs out everyone
highlights.description: Resetting your password now ends every session on your account, on every device. Before, it changed the password and left anyone already signed in where they were.

highlights.title: It disconnects your assistants too
highlights.description: A reset now cuts off Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and any other connected assistant. The app then names each one and shows you how to reconnect it.

highlights.title: Sign out your other devices
highlights.description: A new control on your profile ends every other session on your account. The device you are using stays signed in.

highlights.title: Unused sessions end on their own
highlights.description: A session left alone for 12 hours signs out, and none stays signed in beyond 30 days. You will be asked to sign in more often than before.

releases.title: Clearer signature placement for every signer
releases.summary: Signature, initials and date blocks are placed at a readable size, drawn the way a signer expects, and colour-coded per signer, with undo and remove. An invitation that did not reach the signer is reported instead of shown as sent.

highlights.title: Signing blocks you can read on the page
highlights.description: Each block is sized like an e-signature service places it, with the signer's name above a ruled line. New blocks are laid out clear of each other, not stacked.

highlights.title: Undo, redo, and remove a placed field
highlights.description: A block dragged to the wrong place can be undone, redone, or removed from the field itself, the toolbar, or the Delete key.

highlights.title: Each signer gets their own colour and fields
highlights.description: Every signer has a row with their name, field count and colour, so a two-signer packet shows who signs where. Adding a signer picks a role nobody has taken.

highlights.title: An invitation that did not send says so
highlights.description: When the email to a signer cannot be delivered, the request names the address and the reason instead of reporting that it was sent.

releases.title: Matter folders carry the matter number; automations stay in scope
releases.summary: New matter folders are named with the matter number instead of an internal ID. A workflow rule scoped to one kind of work no longer fires on every matter in its practice. An intake answer too long to store now reaches staff.

highlights.title: Cloud folders are named with the matter number
highlights.description: A new matter's folder reads Smith (CYBE0012) rather than an internal ID. Folders made before this keep their names and stay bound, and the audit recognises both.

highlights.title: Automation rules stay inside the scope you set
highlights.description: A rule scoped to Adoption no longer fires on divorces, or Chapter 7 on Chapter 13. A rule scoped to a whole practice, like Family Law, still covers every matter in it.

highlights.title: An answer too long to store is reported, not dropped
highlights.description: When a client's answer is longer than the field holds, the review task names it and says how long it is, instead of leaving the field quietly empty.

releases.title: Bills you can correct, send, and settle from trust
releases.summary: Draft invoices can be corrected, discounted and emailed to the client, and client funds on retainer settle a bill in one step. Timers ask what you worked on, and firm financial reports are now partner-only.

highlights.title: Correct a bill before the client sees it
highlights.description: Reword, re-price or remove a charge on a draft, and add a discount or flat fee. Removing a charge returns the work to your unbilled queue.

highlights.title: Email an invoice with its PDF
highlights.description: Send the bill to your client from the invoice screen. If delivery fails the invoice stays a draft, so it is never recorded as sent.

highlights.title: Settle a bill from client funds
highlights.description: Apply a retainer to an invoice in one step: the retainer is drawn down and the payment recorded together, with a low balance flagged.

highlights.title: Timers that produce a billable entry
highlights.description: Describe the work on the running timer and it lands ready to bill. Enter time as 1.5, 1:30 or 90m, in your firm's own billing increment.

highlights.title: Financial reports are partner-only
highlights.description: Receivables, realization and work in progress now need billing access. Aging separates invoices not yet due from those overdue.

highlights.title: Editing a time entry or expense date works again
highlights.description: Saving an edited time entry or expense failed whenever the date was included, which was every save. It now saves.

releases.title: Sign and fill inside the document
releases.summary: Clients fill form fields and sign on the document's own signature line in the portal, or upload a signed copy for your review. Paperwork sends your own fee agreement, intake form and questionnaire PDFs. Dropbox Sign is retired.

highlights.title: Sign on the signature line
highlights.description: The portal renders your PDF, places inputs on its form fields, and puts the client's adopted signature on the signature line. PDF fields and printed signature lines are detected.

highlights.title: Or download, sign and upload
highlights.description: A client who prefers paper downloads the form, completes it, and uploads the signed copy. It waits in the E-Signature queue for you to accept or send back.

highlights.title: A filed signed copy, not just a certificate
highlights.description: Every completed request files the filled, signed, flattened PDF to the matter beside the evidence certificate.

highlights.title: Paperwork uses your own forms
highlights.description: Send client paperwork lists the fee agreement, intake form and questionnaire as PDFs you supply, each with a client-signs toggle; requested records are an optional section.

highlights.title: Storage outages no longer fail signing
highlights.description: If the firm's cloud storage is down when a client signs, the signature is kept, the client sees a confirmation, and filing retries automatically while staff see the problem.

highlights.title: One signing provider
highlights.description: The Dropbox Sign option is removed. LawHand's own portal signing is the only provider, so there is nothing to pick or configure.

releases.title: Send any of the three standard pieces
releases.summary: Start this case now lists the fee agreement, questionnaire, and client intake form together, fills the questionnaire with the matter type's own questions, and can send any subset.

highlights.title: The three common pieces, side by side
highlights.description: The fee agreement, client questionnaire, and client intake form are each listed and selectable, so a firm can send one, two, or all three.

highlights.title: A fee agreement is now optional
highlights.description: Send only the questionnaire or requested uploads when no agreement is needed. Signing still opens the portal when an agreement goes out.

highlights.title: Questions match the matter type
highlights.description: The questionnaire starts with the standard questions for the matter type, and the upload hint shows examples for that practice instead of one generic list.

releases.title: Fee agreements fill themselves — drafts can't be approved half-empty
releases.summary: The retainer, its replenishment threshold, the contingency percentage, and the venue in your fee agreement now fill from the matter and its retainer record; a template whose required placeholders nothing can fill can't be approved.

highlights.title: Retainer and contingency terms fill from the matter
highlights.description: The retainer amount, the balance that triggers replenishment, the contingency percentage, and the venue now fill from the matter record and its current retainer.

highlights.title: Matters record their venue
highlights.description: The matter record gains a venue field, set the same way as jurisdiction, so every document that names a forum fills from one place.

highlights.title: Half-empty templates can't be approved
highlights.description: Approving a template now checks that every required placeholder has a record or a default behind it, and jurisdiction terms must name their jurisdiction.

releases.title: Preview the message before you send it
releases.summary: Client paperwork now goes out as a branded email with the firm's name and contact details and a clear portal button, with a separate short text, and the Send step previews both before anything is sent.

highlights.title: See the message before you send it
highlights.description: The Send step shows the exact branded email and short text the client will receive, rendered by the same code that delivers them.

highlights.title: The email looks like your firm
highlights.description: Paperwork now carries your firm's name and contact details and an Open Secure Client Portal button instead of one plain paragraph.

highlights.title: Email and text are separate messages
highlights.description: The full checklist stays in the email; the text is a short line with the link, so the message is readable on any phone.

highlights.title: One link, described correctly
highlights.description: The message no longer promises a second portal link: the invitation link is the portal, and signing the fee agreement unlocks the rest.

releases.title: Intake answers apply to the matter after review
releases.summary: Questionnaire answers propose updates to the contact and matter record (address, phone, case number, court, jurisdiction) for staff to accept. Conflict-of-interest names are checked against firm contacts; nothing changes without approval.

highlights.title: Review questionnaire updates instead of retyping them
highlights.description: Answers that map to the client contact or the matter — address, phone, case number, court, jurisdiction — become changes staff accept or reject, nothing retyped.

highlights.title: Conflicts of interest checked automatically

highlights.title: Nothing changes without staff approval

releases.title: One practice resolver behind routing

highlights.title: One resolver behind routing

highlights.title: The matter record shows its resolved practice

releases.title: Declined signatures and resilient signing

highlights.title: Declines reach the matter
highlights.description: The decline and the client's reason appear on the matter timeline, the chase task closes, and the paperwork drawer marks the form declined.

highlights.title: Signatures survive a storage outage
highlights.description: If cloud storage is briefly unavailable, the client's typed signature is kept and the request finishes on retry without asking them to sign again.

highlights.title: Smoother matter navigation
highlights.description: Opening and moving around a matter no longer trips the rate limit that briefly blocked dashboard, documents, messages and tasks.

releases.title: Prepare paperwork from a firm template

highlights.title: Prepare the fee agreement from a firm template

highlights.title: Add an additional form the same way
highlights.description: The Additional forms card prepares a signing form from a firm template too; it is saved to the matter and checked for signature automatically.

highlights.title: Attach a completed form directly
highlights.description: Additional forms now take a Choose a file upload, so a filled form can be attached without first saving it to the matter's documents.

releases.title: A front door to your client portal
releases.summary: Clients sign in with the email their firm has and a one-time code, the portal carries the firm's own name and contact details, and clients with more than one matter can switch between them.

highlights.title: Sign in with a code, not a password
highlights.description: Enter your email and type the one-time code we send. Sessions last 24 hours, then a fresh code gets you back in, even after the invitation link expires.

highlights.title: The portal looks like your firm, not like software
highlights.description: Your firm's name, logo, phone, email and website now appear on the portal and in the sign-in email, with a "Need help?" footer close at hand.

highlights.title: Always clear which matter you are in
highlights.description: If you have more than one matter, choose one at sign-in and switch any time. Every upload names the matter so documents land in the right place.

releases.title: Start with a 30-day trial

highlights.title: A 30-day trial, set up automatically
highlights.description: Signing up now starts a 30-day trial window, so a new firm can try the platform without a payment step or a setup call.

highlights.title: Premium AI stays off during the trial
highlights.description: Premium AI cannot be switched on until a firm converts, so trial usage stays on the standard models.

highlights.title: Operators are notified and in control
highlights.description: The operator gets a note when a trial starts and can extend, end, or revoke any trial from the platform console.

releases.title: Start paperwork from a filled form

highlights.title: The sample form library works
highlights.description: Template Studio's shared library loads its ready-to-fill starter forms again, ready to preview or fill and download.

highlights.title: Fill the fee agreement in Start this case
highlights.description: Choose a firm template or a shared starter form, fill it out, and attach the finished PDF as the fee agreement or an additional signing form.

releases.title: Live in the matter, miss nothing

highlights.title: Know the moment a client signs

highlights.description: Emailing the client from a matter now fills in the client's email address, and one click inserts the list of records the client still needs to upload.

highlights.title: Client Portal is a main tab
highlights.description: The client portal sits in the matter's primary tabs instead of hiding behind Matter settings, and the client name on a matter links straight to the client record.

releases.title: Say which records you still need

highlights.title: Readable follow-up dates

highlights.title: Calendar names the job
highlights.description: A calendar deadline created from a task now uses the task title instead of its internal type.

releases.title: Texts about the case, only where the client agreed

highlights.title: A text when something needs signing
highlights.description: Where that permission is held, a client is texted as well as emailed when a document is sent for signature. Existing opt-outs still apply.

releases.title: Your sent email is filed with the matter

highlights.title: Matter numbers where you look

highlights.title: Your filters stay put

releases.title: Close a case, and stop losing email attachments

highlights.title: Email attachments become real documents

highlights.title: Documents file themselves

releases.title: Run a case from one page

highlights.title: Watch every document until it is signed
highlights.description: One strip shows each document, what is outstanding, what the client returned, and any message that did not arrive.

highlights.title: Give any document a due date

highlights.title: A calmer matter page
highlights.description: Overview, Documents, Activity, and Billing are the page you work from. Team, Workflow, and the portal group under Matter settings.

releases.title: Browse sample legal forms in Template Studio

highlights.description: Preview and fill a sample form directly from the library without saving a copy.

highlights.title: Your firm's templates stay separate
highlights.description: Sample forms are read-only shared content; your own templates and drafts are left untouched.

highlights.description: Portal users get the same heads-up as firm staff, so a brief maintenance message never comes as a surprise.

releases.title: Every matter now has a number you can say out loud

releases.title: Standard client paperwork for every new matter

releases.title: Prepare client paperwork from the matter workspace
