highlights.title: Prepare templates and email attachments
highlights.description: Draw named fields and whiteout areas in Studio. Review files before emailing them, and copy documents into another folder without changing the source.

releases.title: Save reviewed Word-to-PDF documents reliably

highlights.description: Save a reviewed Word-to-PDF document without a false mismatch caused by its internal file timestamps. Changed values still require a fresh preview.

releases.title: Review generated PDFs directly in Studio

highlights.description: Generated PDF and Word-to-PDF previews include page navigation, fit-to-width and zoom, with clear loading and error messages.

highlights.title: Finish missing information faster
highlights.description: Keep required blanks and unreviewed suggestions visible, move through the current review queue, and open firm or matter details to correct the source without losing entered values.

releases.title: Review long Word templates with confidence

highlights.title: Keep long documents reviewable
highlights.description: Long Word imports retain more complete source context. Jump directly to a page and move between document and fields on smaller screens.

releases.title: Prepare recurring matter work with named service identities

highlights.description: Daily, weekly, and approved lifecycle-event schedules create durable proposals with the approving attorney as reviewer. Existing review controls still decide every final action.

releases.title: See connected assistant activity across your firm

highlights.title: Recover without duplicate documents

releases.title: Keep signing fields ready for e-signing

releases.title: Prepare workflow drafts from your firm's history

releases.title: Prepare workflows from everyday firm events

highlights.title: Prepare for deadlines and overdue invoices
highlights.description: Watch deadlines within three days and unpaid overdue invoices. Duplicate events prepare one run; changed facts block preparation. Applying a workflow still requires approval.

releases.title: Work directly on documents in Template Studio
releases.summary: See more of the document, place PDF fields where you click, and revise Word wording while keeping mapped fields.

releases.title: Reuse shared firm details in templates

highlights.title: See shared values and missing setup

releases.title: Review exact document revisions before delivery
releases.summary: Review assistant documents in a staff-and-attorney sequence or an attorney-only sequence, with a lasting record of the exact file approved.

highlights.description: Choose the review sequence for new drafts. Assigned reviewers can approve, request changes, or record a reasoned attorney override in chat and the work board.

highlights.title: Send the reviewed document

releases.title: Reuse templates and finish matter fields faster

highlights.description: Copy a saved document and its fields into an independent draft without uploading the sample again.

releases.title: Bound connected assistant usage

releases.title: Restore Word previews in Template Studio

highlights.title: Ask a question, then narrow
highlights.description: One search box and a scope choice replace six filters. Matter, source, file type and dates now sit behind Refine, and anything you set stays visible as a chip you can remove.

highlights.title: Find old records nobody linked to a matter
highlights.description: A research question no longer has to match every word in one passage, so a half-remembered phrase finds a document filed years ago. Quoted phrases and AND, OR and NOT still work.

highlights.title: See what was searched
highlights.description: Matched words are highlighted in every result. A complete search says so, and an incomplete one names the reason and who can clear it.

releases.title: Transfer client folders through the portal
releases.summary: Send multiple files and folders with per-file results, share cloud transfer links, and refresh matter document lists.

highlights.title: Bring a folder of documents
highlights.description: Clients can select or drop files and folders into their invited matter, preserve subfolders, and retry failed files. Reselecting unchanged source files avoids duplicate uploads.

highlights.title: Use a shared folder
highlights.description: Clients can send a source link for legal-team review. Staff can explicitly publish a client-safe upload-folder link in the portal.

highlights.title: Refresh the document list
highlights.description: Refresh saved document lists after uploads. Connected cloud-folder sync remains separate; saving or refreshing files does not mean content indexing or OCR is complete.

releases.title: A workspace view for every role
releases.summary: Give staff a focused workspace and let each person arrange their own navigation.

highlights.title: Choose functions by role
highlights.description: Administrators can configure role view profiles using Receptionist, Finance, Secretary, Paralegal, Attorney, and Partner starting points, then assign those roles to staff.

highlights.title: Make navigation your own
highlights.description: Use the navigation gear to hide and reorder available functions or restore role defaults. Your saved layout follows your account on desktop and phone.

releases.title: Correct everyday work and keep your place
releases.summary: Edit task details, return to the right matter section, and recover from estate-entry errors while reducing unnecessary background work.

highlights.title: Keep the selected work in view
highlights.description: Return to the right matter section with bookmarks and browser Back. Document review returns to Documents, and new tasks inherit the selected matter.

highlights.title: Correct work and recover from interruptions
highlights.description: Correct task details and clear dates without recreating work. Estate forms explain errors and retain failed drafts. Intake recovery and Studio Undo are more reliable.

highlights.title: Use fewer resources
highlights.description: Assistant lists load where they are used, portal message polling waits for pending reads, directory sync reuses user lookups, and oversized chat attachment reads are bounded.

releases.title: Keep new-client intake moving from paperwork to meeting
releases.summary: Start a reviewed fee agreement and client questionnaire from Create Matter, deliver secure portal invitations by email or SMS, and track document and meeting follow-ups.

highlights.title: Start intake as part of matter creation
highlights.description: Authorized attorneys, paralegals and secretaries can prepare the packet, choose email or SMS and assign responsible staff.

highlights.title: Wait for both completed documents
highlights.description: The signed agreement and questionnaire are tracked independently. Both completed requirements close the seven-day follow-up and create a scheduling task due within 24 hours.

highlights.title: Work with Microsoft 365 or Google
highlights.description: Use connected email and storage, existing staff task calendars and the secure client portal. Review uncertain delivery and record a conference call or in-person meeting.

releases.title: Bring existing matters and historical email into LawHand
releases.summary: Import USB folders or ZIP files from New Matter, review client and matter mappings, and preserve historical emails in Correspondence.

highlights.title: Create many matters from folders
highlights.description: Authorized staff review folder mappings, clients and intake stages before creating matters.

highlights.title: Preserve former-firm email
highlights.description: EML messages retain their original files and appear in Correspondence without requiring a matching email domain.

highlights.title: Resume incomplete imports
highlights.description: Review each file result and retry unfinished uploads using the saved import ID.

releases.title: Keep everyday casework within reach on your phone
releases.summary: Matter pages now put notes, documents, tasks, workflow review and client contact together on small screens, with visible note-save recovery.

highlights.title: Reach your matter work quickly
highlights.description: Choose any matter section from a phone-friendly picker, see the current stage and open tasks, or jump directly to documents, review and client contact.

highlights.title: Retry a note without duplicating it
highlights.description: Interrupted note saves keep text on the open page. Confirmed saves show a receipt; retrying the same request creates one note and activity event.

highlights.title: Know where a file can open
highlights.description: Phone users see the Windows network-file opener limitation and can use existing permitted document or provider links. Email forms fit shorter screens.

releases.title: Keep workflow preparation visible and recoverable
releases.summary: Matter workflow rules now queue preparation reliably with the matter save and show progress through review.

highlights.title: Recover interrupted planning
highlights.description: Queued workflow preparation retries temporary failures without duplicating a reviewed run.

highlights.title: Review prepared work from the matter
highlights.description: See pending, retrying, planned, blocked and failed activity, then open a prepared run before explicitly approving it.

highlights.title: Recheck changed facts and permissions
highlights.description: Changed matter facts, rules, templates or actor permissions require a fresh manual review instead of silently replaying old events.

releases.title: See the limits of research evidence
releases.summary: Research checks source jurisdiction before treating a requested location as covered and keeps source capture details visible with cited authorities.

highlights.title: Know which jurisdiction a source supports
highlights.description: Wrong-jurisdiction and unknown-jurisdiction hits no longer fill a requested coverage gap.

highlights.title: Inspect source dates and status
highlights.description: Cited public sources show catalogue status, retrieval and sync dates, and unknown values. These details do not establish current law or treatment.

releases.title: Keep approved templates available while preparing the next version
releases.summary: Template Studio keeps the published wording available during draft edits and adds reviewed matter-document details and clearer scenario selection.

highlights.title: Draft without interrupting the team
highlights.description: Test the next draft separately while colleagues generate from the last published version.

highlights.title: Review details from source documents
highlights.description: Find labeled details in Word, PDF and text matter documents, correct them, then explicitly accept them into supported matter fields. Existing values require confirmation.

highlights.title: Choose the right scenario
highlights.description: Name a scenario and require a matching saved matter or client detail, including Yes/No answers, before generating. Missing details stay unresolved.

releases.title: Firm Memory keeps native file permissions intact
releases.summary: Firm Memory now withholds results when native file authorization cannot be established. An opt-in on-premises OpenSearch path connects document extraction and portal search with permission and freshness checks.

highlights.title: Unavailable authorization stays private
highlights.description: An offline or unhealthy file-search agent no longer falls back to cloud filenames and snippets when native permissions are required.

highlights.title: A bounded on-premises search pilot
highlights.description: Configured nodes use isolated extraction and OpenSearch, checking live file access before returning results. Customer-scale and OCR acceptance require a rehearsal.

releases.title: Take a Word template all the way to signature
releases.summary: Template Studio can now turn a completed Word template into a reviewed PDF without losing the editable DOCX option, closing the handoff from document preparation to e-signature.

highlights.title: Choose editable or ready to sign
highlights.description: Generate an editable Word document for another drafting pass, or choose PDF for signature when the document is final.

highlights.title: Review the exact PDF before saving
highlights.description: The converted PDF opens in the Studio preview and is bound to its matter and field values before the final matter file is created.

highlights.title: Keep conversion bounded and validated
highlights.description: Word conversion runs with time, size, and page limits in a private workspace, and active or malformed PDF output is rejected.

releases.title: Test and publish the exact template your firm approved
releases.summary: Template Studio now separates drafting, testing, publishing, and pausing. Every version number names exact immutable wording, and matter generation refuses anything except the published version.

highlights.title: Test before your team can generate
highlights.description: A draft must render successfully with representative values before an authorized user can publish that exact version.

highlights.title: Know exactly which wording was used
highlights.description: Every edit creates an immutable resulting version, and matter generation records and verifies the published version instead of trusting a changing draft.

highlights.title: Work queues that match the whole library
highlights.description: Continue setup, source problems, awaiting publication, and published queues now use firm-wide results rather than whichever page happens to be open.

releases.title: Templates that fill themselves and keep their history
releases.summary: Template fields can say where their value comes from, clauses can appear only when they apply, repeating sections scale with the matter's parties, and every published version is kept so you can restore an earlier wording.

highlights.title: Tell a field where its value comes from
highlights.description: Pick a data source for each field — case number, client address, plaintiff, attorney — and it fills from the matter every time, whatever you named it.

highlights.title: One template instead of near-identical copies
highlights.description: Mark a clause to appear only when a field applies, with {{#if}} in the document itself. Two near-identical templates become one.

highlights.title: Repeating sections that follow the matter
highlights.description: Wrap a block in {{#each parties}} and it renders once per party on the matter — a signature block each — with no editing afterwards.

highlights.title: Version history with restore
highlights.description: Every saved state has its own exact version number. The Versions tab shows what changed and restores an earlier version as a new draft without retyping it.

highlights.title: Mark up Word templates by hand
highlights.description: See the document itself: highlight text to make it a field, and select paragraphs to make them conditional or repeat once per party.

releases.title: Plan matter workflows automatically, approve them the same way
releases.summary: Firms can have an approved workflow template prepared the moment a matter opens or reaches a stage. The automation only prepares the work; a reviewer still approves and applies it.

highlights.title: Two bounded triggers, one action
highlights.description: A rule fires when a matter is opened or enters a named stage, optionally narrowed by matter type or practice area, and plans one approved workflow template. Nothing else.

highlights.title: Automation is approved like legal work
highlights.description: A rule is created as a draft and does nothing until an approver activates the exact definition they reviewed. Editing a rule returns it to draft for a fresh approval.

highlights.title: Nothing is applied without a person
highlights.description: A matching rule creates the same reviewable preview the Workflow tab creates by hand. Tasks and matter stages change only when someone applies the planned run.

highlights.title: A rule that does nothing says why
highlights.description: Every match is recorded as immutable evidence naming the rule, the matter, and the planned run, or the reason it was blocked. The matter's Workflow tab shows it too.

releases.title: Firm-wide Firm Memory research that opens the document
releases.summary: Firm Memory research now searches document text across every matter you are authorized on, says what it could not cover, and every on-premise result opens to its matter file.

highlights.title: Ask without picking a matter first
highlights.description: A query with no matter filter searches the matters on each file share you are already authorized on, decided by the same matter policy a chosen matter goes through.

highlights.title: Search inside documents, not just file names
highlights.description: Results come from the firm's own search node with real page numbers and passages; if that node cannot be reached, the response says so.

highlights.title: Open every result you find
highlights.description: An on-premise result links to its matter file, which rechecks the matter binding, the live index entry, and the bound folder before showing it.

highlights.title: Know what a search did not cover
highlights.description: Every incomplete response states in one sentence why, so “no matches” is only ever said about a search that actually covered its sources.

releases.title: Organize matter documents with folders and tags
releases.summary: Case documents get a file-explorer view: a per-matter folder tree, firm-wide tags, search and sort, and uploads that write into the matching folder of the firm's bound cloud share.

highlights.title: Group case files into folders
highlights.description: Each matter has its own folder tree with drag-and-drop filing, breadcrumbs, and per-folder counts. Deleting a folder never deletes the documents inside it.

highlights.title: Label documents across matters
highlights.description: Firm-wide tags apply to any case document and filter the list conjunctively, so “Signed” plus “Filed” narrows to documents carrying both.

highlights.title: Find a document without scrolling
highlights.description: Filename and description search, folder scoping with or without subfolders, and name, date, or size sorting all run on the server rather than in the browser.

highlights.title: The cloud share mirrors the same tree
highlights.description: A document uploaded into a folder is written to the matching folder under the matter in the firm's cloud share, and portal uploads file themselves into Client Uploads.

releases.title: Consent-aware SMS with review and opt-out controls
releases.summary: Firms can configure provider-backed SMS that stays reviewable, consent-bound, tenant-scoped, and honest about provider acceptance and delivery.

highlights.title: Send only with current consent
highlights.description: Each outbound message rechecks verified phone ownership, consent provenance, approved message category, quiet hours, matter access, and provider configuration.

highlights.title: Honor replies and opt-outs safely
highlights.description: Signed inbound messages require an active owned sender, handle STOP, START, and HELP, deduplicate retries, and route ambiguous matches to staff review.

highlights.title: Keep provider truth distinct
highlights.description: Exact-generation callbacks and reconciliation update authorized timeline evidence without regressing known truth; provider acceptance remains distinct from confirmed delivery.

highlights.title: Review assistant proposals first
highlights.description: Workspace SMS proposals require current matter access and an explicit retry key, stay inside LawHand instead of email or third-party calendars, and cannot dispatch autonomously.

releases.title: Secure opening for on-premise Firm Memory files
releases.summary: When a firm explicitly enables the Windows helper, authorized Firm Memory results can open through the signed-in user's Windows session without placing a network path in a browser link.

highlights.title: Open with one-time authorization
highlights.description: Each action uses a short-lived, single-use request bound to the tenant, user, source file, assigned agent, revision, and requested action.

highlights.title: Keep network paths local
highlights.description: The browser and launch link carry no UNC, file, or SMB path; the local agent resolves the opaque source identity only after redemption.

highlights.title: Honor current Windows access
highlights.description: Windows rechecks reachability and the signed-in user's SMB/NTFS access; moved, expired, offline, and denied requests fail closed with a copy-path fallback.

releases.title: Durable Template Studio preview processing
releases.summary: Template Studio now has a tenant-isolated durable job and artifact foundation for reliable preview and test-render processing.

highlights.title: Resume interrupted work
highlights.description: Preview and test-render requests use durable queued jobs with bounded retries, cancellation, lease recovery, and tenant-safe status resources.

highlights.title: Keep evidence exact
highlights.description: Completed output is hash-verified and can become current evidence only when the immutable snapshot, draft revision, and identity still match.

highlights.title: Protect private document data
highlights.description: Job metadata excludes document values, bytes, storage paths, provider identifiers, signed URLs, and raw exception text.

highlights.title: Keep activation review-gated
highlights.description: The production worker remains disabled until encrypted CAS backup and restore rehearsal are added to the release gate.

releases.title: Revalidate authority evidence before alerts
releases.summary: Public-authority alerts and coverage claims now remain bound to the exact reviewed evidence lineage and source state that supported them.

highlights.title: Stop revoked evidence from sending
highlights.description: Queued authority alerts recheck the stored history or citation fact and both public source lineages before recording a successful delivery.

highlights.title: Keep coverage claims audit-bound
highlights.description: Changes to coverage scope, source identity, publisher, URLs, cadence, caveats, or other customer-visible source facts suppress claims until fresh audits pass.

highlights.title: Reject mismatched citation identities
highlights.description: Citation facts must link each opinion to the same reviewed source as its authority, preventing unrelated public opinions from laundering revoked or private evidence.

releases.title: Fail-closed public-authority source boundaries
releases.summary: Public legal research now serves and describes only reviewed official, open, or licensed sources that are explicitly admitted to the promoted authority release.

highlights.title: Require explicit public admission
highlights.description: A source key or caller-supplied metadata cannot make legal documents or case law public; the reviewed catalog, admission, and promoted manifest must agree.

highlights.title: Suppress revoked or mismatched sources
highlights.description: Source-rights, review, storage, schema, implementation, namespace, or manifest changes immediately suppress public results, status, coverage, and claims.

highlights.title: Keep private firm data out
highlights.description: Tenant, firm, private, custom, and unknown records cannot enter the public-authority corpus, telemetry, counts, audits, or customer coverage projection.

releases.title: Reliable file-share agent setup on managed Windows networks
releases.summary: The LawHand file-share agent now uses Windows-managed certificate trust when connecting to LawHand, improving enrollment reliability on firms' inspected HTTPS networks.

highlights.title: Enroll without weakening TLS
highlights.description: The agent recognizes approved enterprise certificate authorities deployed by the firm's Windows administrators while continuing to validate the LawHand hostname and certificate.

highlights.title: Keep the same secure connection
highlights.description: No inbound network access or certificate-validation bypass is required; the agent continues to use outbound HTTPS for its assigned file-share work.

releases.title: Configurable matter workflows with reviewable runs
releases.summary: Firms can define bounded matter data and apply approved stage and checklist templates through previewed, auditable workflow runs.

highlights.title: Model firm-specific matter data
highlights.description: Administrators can define typed matter fields with stable keys, required and sensitive handling, bounded options, and safe retirement controls in the matter workflow surface.

highlights.title: Preview before applying a workflow
highlights.description: Approved matter templates show the exact initial stage, required data, assignee gaps, checklist tasks, and snapshot hash before any matter or task changes occur.

highlights.title: Apply once with durable evidence
highlights.description: Approved runs create deterministic relative tasks in one transaction, reject stale previews, deduplicate retries, and retain immutable run and step evidence.

highlights.title: Compensate without erasing history
highlights.description: Rollback cancels only unchanged workflow-created tasks, restores the prior matter stage, reports blockers for manual review, and keeps authoring separate from legal approval.

releases.title: Template Studio workspaces and resumable setup
releases.summary: Document templates now have a first-class Studio home, persistent workspaces, and clearer paths from source preparation to generation.

highlights.title: Resume template setup
highlights.description: Studio home groups loaded templates into continue setup, needs attention, ready to generate, and recent views using the existing library status.

highlights.title: Open a persistent workspace
highlights.description: Every template links to a stable workspace for reviewing its source, fields, readiness, preview, and generation actions.

highlights.title: Keep source preparation intact
highlights.description: New and imported templates continue through the reviewed Word, PDF, and image preparation flow before opening their workspace.

highlights.title: See current limits clearly
highlights.description: Reserved test, version, activity, draft, proposal, and snapshot routes say when server-backed records are not yet available instead of showing fake controls.

releases.title: Shared research workspaces with reviewable evidence
releases.summary: Matter teams can now preserve a shared research trail without turning machine notes into source evidence.

highlights.title: Keep the team trail together
highlights.description: Create matter-scoped workspaces for saved issues, searches, authorities, highlights, annotations, exclusions, outlines, and memo notes with explicit member roles.

highlights.title: Carry evidence labels forward
highlights.description: Every saved item and frozen export keeps its cited, verify, or model label alongside exact source links, source version, pinpoints, and stored treatment/currentness state.

highlights.title: Freeze a review package
highlights.description: Immutable, hash-identified snapshots create an exportable record of the workspace as reviewed. Bluebook formatting and citation correctness still require attorney verification.

highlights.title: Revoke safely
highlights.description: Workspace access is tenant-and-matter scoped, role checked, auditable, and revocable; archived workspaces and records are retained rather than silently erased.

releases.title: Review-first citator evidence controls
releases.summary: Research now separates linked source facts from provisional treatment interpretation and makes citator limits visible before attorney review.

highlights.title: Inspect the evidence state
highlights.description: Citator results show the promoted source, version, as-of date, history or citation evidence, and currentness limitations separately from any machine interpretation.

highlights.title: Keep treatment reviewable
highlights.description: Machine labels may abstain and remain provisional until an attorney accepts, rejects, requests more evidence, or records an override in the append-only review trail.

highlights.title: Watch changes safely
highlights.description: Saved authority watches are consented, tenant-and-matter scoped, deduplicated, revocable, and ready for quiet-hour and failure-aware delivery. This release sends no alerts.

highlights.title: No unsupported status claim
highlights.description: LawHand does not call an authority good law from a missing negative record. Complete citator coverage still requires a permitted licensed or attorney-reviewed benchmark.

releases.title: Private mediation review and party-specific sharing
releases.summary: Licensed mediation work now appears inside the client's existing matter portal while documents and proposals stay private until attorney review and deliberate release.

highlights.title: Keep each submission private
highlights.description: A party's document or proposal is visible to that party and the firm until the legal team explicitly releases it to selected recipients.

highlights.title: Review before delivery
highlights.description: Attorneys can approve, return, or reject proposals before choosing who receives an approved version; released content is preserved as immutable evidence.

highlights.title: Negotiate with traceable counters
highlights.description: Counteroffers can reference only an active proposal released to that party, and the prior offer is superseded only when the reviewed counter is actually released.

highlights.title: Use mediation in My Matters
highlights.description: Eligible clients see a read-only Mediation tab in their native matter portal, with scoped assets, proposals, and integrity-checked document downloads when the add-on is active.

releases.title: Clearer legal research gaps
releases.summary: Research now separates linked source facts from provisional treatment interpretation and makes citator limits visible before attorney review.

highlights.title: Keep verified findings
highlights.description: When a response mixes cited and unsupported material, cited findings remain visible while unsupported claims are omitted.

highlights.title: Explain missing authority
highlights.description: Research gaps now say whether the authority service or fallback was unavailable, or whether no usable match was found.

highlights.title: Open the cited source
highlights.description: CourtListener and official public-source URLs remain attached to the cited source so reviewers can open the retrieved authority.

highlights.title: Avoid uncited legal summaries
highlights.description: Jurisdiction-specific questions without authority no longer receive a general-knowledge answer presented as completed research.

releases.title: Versioned public-authority coverage
releases.summary: Public legal research now exposes reviewed source scope, corpus release evidence, currentness limits, and honest retrieval fallbacks.

highlights.title: See reviewed source scope
highlights.description: Rights decisions, authority tiers, content types, jurisdictions, temporal scope, cadence, caveats, and provenance are carried with source health.

highlights.title: Track corpus releases honestly
highlights.description: Promoted versions, rollback metadata, harvest checkpoints, quarantine states, and sampled audits prevent unsupported complete/current claims.

highlights.title: Preserve retrieval boundaries
highlights.description: Exact embedding compatibility is required; outages or mismatches fall back to keyword/source search while private firm documents remain outside public telemetry.

releases.title: Controlled client and matter import promotion
releases.summary: Administrators can approve an unchanged import report before promoting the conservative client and matter subset, with durable links and rollback review markers.

highlights.title: Approve the exact reconciliation
highlights.description: Promotion requires an explicit confirmation and report hash, so changed or stale staging cannot be promoted silently.

highlights.title: Reconcile existing records
highlights.description: Client identifiers and email addresses are matched within the tenant before a new client is created; every promoted row receives an external provenance link.

highlights.title: Keep rollback reviewable
highlights.description: Operators can mark a promoted run for non-destructive rollback review while audit receipts preserve what happened.

releases.title: Search a firm's local case-file memory
releases.summary: A bounded local file-search control surface connects an approved file-share agent to the portal, Chat, and Workspace MCP while keeping the firm's query and documents on the firm's network.

highlights.title: Search inside supported local files
highlights.description: Matter-scoped searches can return ranked snippets and page hints from the agent's local SQLite control index without embeddings.

highlights.title: Use the same search from three surfaces
highlights.description: The portal, Chat assistant, and user-authorized Workspace MCP now share one bounded search contract with visible partial and index status.

highlights.title: Open results safely
highlights.description: Results use an authenticated portal link that rechecks access and offers Copy UNC instead of exposing a raw browser file link.

highlights.title: Measure the pilot honestly
highlights.description: Correlation IDs, counts, latency, and indexed or pending status support local validation; this remains a small control-index PoC, not a 4 TB production search promise.

releases.title: Deeper federal and Ohio research coverage
releases.summary: Research can ingest reviewed federal rules, constitutional analysis, and Tax Court reports while keeping jurisdiction and known extraction limits explicit.

highlights.title: Search more reviewed federal authority
highlights.description: Federal rules, Constitution Annotated, and bounded Tax Court Reports now have scheduled, failure-isolated ingestion paths.

highlights.title: Keep unsafe text out
highlights.description: A known unreadable appellate-rules extraction stays auditable but cannot enter searchable text until its parser is replaced.

highlights.title: Scope Ohio and federal research correctly
highlights.description: Explicit Ohio and federal questions now apply matching filters to case law and other public authorities.

releases.title: Review-first Brief Check
releases.summary: Firms can review brief citations, quotations, pin cites, opposing-brief differences, and bounded authority candidates with linked evidence before exporting work product.

highlights.title: Inspect evidence before relying on a brief
highlights.description: DOCX/PDF checks preserve source identity, location, confidence, ambiguity, retrieval evidence, and explicit unknown or unavailable states.

highlights.title: Keep attorney decisions auditable
highlights.description: Reviewers can accept, reject, or follow up on findings; decisions are tenant-scoped and recorded in an immutable audit trail.

highlights.title: Export linked review work product
highlights.description: Download a review report and table-of-authorities draft while bounded recall and currentness limitations remain visible.

releases.title: Operating trust workflows and evidence
releases.summary: Customers and operators can use one versioned contract for support, incidents, lifecycle receipts, offboarding proof, providers, and security review without unsupported SLA or certification claims.

highlights.title: Use defined support and status workflows
highlights.description: Published business hours, S1-S4 severity objectives, audited escalation, and sanitized append-only incident updates make the operating process reviewable without creating an SLA.

highlights.title: Carry acceptance evidence through the lifecycle
highlights.description: Onboarding, BK28 migration, and export receipts reconcile scope and counts; offboarding blocks on holds and needs two operators before proof.

highlights.title: Export an honest security packet
highlights.description: The content-addressed packet names providers and boundaries while marking penetration testing and certifications as not attained.

releases.title: Attributed intake and safer lead follow-through
releases.summary: Firms can capture attributed public inquiries, triage conflicts, book consultations, and follow up with explicit consent while keeping the conversion trail auditable.

highlights.title: Capture inquiries safely
highlights.description: Conditional forms accept only validated answers, resist simple spam, preserve source attribution, and deduplicate retries.

highlights.title: Review before conversion
highlights.description: Public leads require an explicit conflict decision before they can become matters; appointment booking and reminder state remain durable.

highlights.title: Respect communication choices
highlights.description: Authored email follow-up checks current consent and reports provider failure truthfully; SMS remains unavailable until its compliance controls are ready.

releases.title: Zoom Phone setup now shows exactly what needs attention
releases.summary: Tenant administrators can follow Zoom Phone setup stage by stage and recover from authorization failures without leaving the integration panel.

highlights.title: See each setup stage
highlights.description: The Zoom panel separately tracks saved app credentials, account authorization, Phone API permissions, and verified real-time call delivery.

highlights.title: Recover from the actual authorization problem
highlights.description: Zoom authorization returns to the integration panel with specific guidance for rejected credentials, expired requests, missing permissions, and account mismatches.

highlights.title: Know when reconnecting is required
highlights.description: Replacing an OAuth client pair now clearly reports that the previous grant was disconnected and directs the administrator to authorize the current app.

releases.title: Client portal payments and durable sign-in
releases.summary: Clients can activate a durable portal account, pay an invoice through hosted Stripe Checkout, and complete certified Dropbox Sign requests when the firm configures the provider.

highlights.title: Pay invoices securely
highlights.description: The portal opens a hosted Stripe Checkout session for the current invoice balance; payment status updates only after verified provider reconciliation.

highlights.title: Return with durable sign-in
highlights.description: Clients can activate a password-backed account and sign into an explicitly selected matter while invitation revocation remains authoritative.

highlights.title: Use certified e-signature providers
highlights.description: Dropbox Sign dispatch and signed or declined webhook events are authenticated, tenant-bound, and idempotently reconciled.

releases.title: Zoom Phone setup now shows the exact authorization path
releases.summary: Tenant administrators can configure Zoom Phone with the exact required permissions and start authorization from the correct LawHand control.

highlights.title: Choose only the required Phone access
highlights.description: The Zoom setup panel names both account call-history permissions, shows their exact identifiers, and links directly to Zoom's Call Logs reference.

highlights.title: Start the secure tenant connection correctly
highlights.description: LawHand now warns administrators to use Connect Zoom Phone instead of Marketplace Add or generated authorization links, preserving the tenant-bound authorization check.

releases.title: Demo workspaces are clearly identified for operators
releases.summary: Platform operators can now distinguish disposable demo workspaces from regular platform tenants in the tenant inventory.

highlights.title: See the tenant type
highlights.description: The platform tenant list labels each workspace as Demo or Platform without using the billing tier as the visible grouping.

highlights.title: See demo expiry at a glance
highlights.description: Demo rows show their expiration and clearly flag workspaces that have already expired.

highlights.title: Filter the inventory
highlights.description: Operators can focus the tenant list on demo workspaces or regular platform tenants while the dedicated demo controls remain protected.

highlights.title: Use Zen free background capacity
highlights.description: Platform operators can assign OpenCode Zen free models to the Background Automations route while Standard and Premium keep their confidential-data safeguards.

releases.title: The platform tour now follows a matter end to end
releases.summary: The LawHand platform tour now shows how legal work moves from intake and conflict review through preparation, client action, signature, billing, and follow-through.

highlights.title: Follow the matter
highlights.description: Step through a visual workflow from the first call to an opened matter, attorney review, client delivery, and accounting.

highlights.title: See every role's handoff
highlights.description: Compare what attorneys, paralegals, intake staff, billing staff, and clients need from the same matter record.

highlights.title: Evaluate the complete platform
highlights.description: Review expanded capability, practice-area, integration, and control sections with clear rollout labels and concrete workflow details.

releases.title: Product claims now show rollout and research boundaries
releases.summary: LawHand product and pricing pages now distinguish shipped behavior, controlled pilots, planned work, and provider-dependent connections.

highlights.title: See the rollout state
highlights.description: Capability cards identify implemented behavior, controlled pilots, and connections that require a separate provider account or approval.

highlights.title: Evaluate Research MCP as a pilot
highlights.description: Research MCP pricing and product pages now state the controlled-pilot gate and the configured public-authority coverage boundary.

highlights.title: Keep research claims precise
highlights.description: LawHand explains that source links support attorney review without claiming Westlaw replacement, comprehensive coverage, or a good-law determination.

releases.title: Agreement evidence and safer retention controls
releases.summary: Firms can review current agreement acceptance evidence and preview safe expiry cleanup with legal-hold protection.

highlights.title: Know what was accepted
highlights.description: Tenant admins can review counsel-owned agreement versions and record signer, authority, and immutable document evidence.

highlights.title: Retention with guardrails
highlights.description: Review tenant data-store inventory, configure retention, preview cleanup, and protect held or matter data from deletion.

releases.title: Research API keys put staff access and spend under firm control
releases.summary: Firm administrators can provision LawHand Research keys for staff, bound their lifetime and budget, and see usage and charges from the MCP portal.

highlights.title: Issue keys with clear custody
highlights.description: Name each key, record its purpose, assign it to a LawHand staff profile, and choose exactly which Research tools it may use.

highlights.title: Bound time and spend
highlights.description: Set an expiration, monthly dollar budget, call cap, and burst limit; the gateway stops successful calls before they exceed either hard monthly boundary.

highlights.title: See the complete key ledger
highlights.description: The portal shows active, expired, and revoked keys with creator, custodian, last use, successful and failed calls, current-month charges, and remaining budget.

highlights.title: Connect standard API clients
highlights.description: LawHand Research keys work as standard Bearer credentials while the existing custom header remains supported for compatible clients.

releases.title: Document automation is faster, safer, and easier to manage
releases.summary: Firms can navigate larger template libraries, see readiness at a glance, and keep reviewed document generation moving with stronger recovery controls.

highlights.title: Find the right template faster
highlights.description: Search titles and descriptions, filter by status or category, and move through a paged library without loading every template at once.

highlights.title: See what needs attention
highlights.description: Library health cards distinguish ready templates, drafts, and binary templates whose original source must be restored before use.

highlights.title: Keep concurrent work moving
highlights.description: Independent scans and tenant background work can progress within bounded capacity instead of waiting behind one unrelated long-running job.

highlights.title: Save the reviewed PDFΓÇönot a surprise
highlights.description: Final PDF saves recheck the exact reviewed output and clean up or quarantine staged files when storage and database results cannot be proven consistent.

releases.title: Connected assistants can prepare complete matter work for review
releases.summary: Claude, Codex, ChatGPT, and other approved Workspace MCP clients can now gather client-to-task context, read matter documents and templates, and place prepared documents into LawHand's staged review workflow.

highlights.title: Gather the working context
highlights.description: Approved assistants can search clients, intakes, matters, and tasks, then load parties, team, events, notes, communications, and history within the user's permissions.

highlights.title: Reason over documents and templates
highlights.description: The assistant can read bounded text from uploaded matter documents and approved templates, including the template's fillable-field contract.

highlights.title: Send prepared documents through human review
highlights.description: Fresh or template-rendered Word documents go to tenant cloud with a LawHand Review task for staff and attorney approval. Assistants cannot approve, file, send, or deliver.

highlights.title: Reconnect older one-tool connections
highlights.description: Connections that still show only Find matter keep their original consent. Remove and reconnect once to review expanded scopes; LawHand never enlarges grants silently.

releases.title: Research connections now complete authorization
releases.summary: Claude, ChatGPT, and other hosted clients can now complete the LawHand Research authorization screen without supplying a separate API key.

highlights.title: Approve the connection in LawHand
highlights.description: After adding the Research MCP URL, sign in and approve research-only access through the normal LawHand authorization page.

highlights.title: No pasted key for hosted clients
highlights.description: Hosted clients register securely and use OAuth; Research API keys remain an option only for clients that support custom headers.

releases.title: Plaintiff and defendant fields are clear and reusable
releases.summary: Matter parties now distinguish caption roles from the client relationship, and document templates can Smart Fill reviewed singular or multi-party plaintiff and defendant names.

highlights.title: Identify the actual caption role
highlights.description: The Parties tab now defines plaintiff, defendant, petitioner, and respondent alongside client, counsel, witness, and expert roles.

highlights.title: Choose the primary named party
highlights.description: For matters with multiple plaintiffs or defendants, staff can mark the primary contact used by a singular template field.

highlights.title: Reuse parties safely in documents
highlights.description: Templates can use explicit singular and plural plaintiff or defendant fields, with every Smart Fill value still reviewed before preview or save.

releases.title: Integration administration is organized in one clear workspace
releases.summary: Administrators can now review every connected service from one Integrations workspace with clearer purpose, permissions, setup requirements, and operating guides.

highlights.title: Find every connection in Integrations
highlights.description: Cloud accounts, search, file shares, Teams, Zoom, QuickBooks, and MCP now live under one organized administrative workspace.

highlights.title: Understand access before setup
highlights.description: Each integration explains what it does, the data and permissions it uses, and the prerequisites an administrator should confirm.

highlights.title: Move from overview to the right controls
highlights.description: Focused sections keep configuration close at hand, while expandable notes link directly to the relevant administrative guide.

releases.title: QuickBooks invoice sync is smoother and respects tax choices
releases.summary: QuickBooks connections now return directly to LawHand, account setup is more reliable, and each invoice's sales-tax choice carries into QuickBooks.

highlights.title: Return directly to QuickBooks settings
highlights.description: After approving the connection in Intuit, administrators land back in LawHand with a clear connected confirmation.

highlights.title: Configure accounts without losing other mappings
highlights.description: Accounts-receivable settings save correctly, and a temporary catalogue error no longer hides every available QuickBooks option.

highlights.title: Keep non-taxable legal services non-taxable
highlights.description: An invoice with a zero sales-tax rate sends non-taxable lines to QuickBooks; a positive rate sends taxable lines.

releases.title: Signature requests are easier to deliver and follow through
releases.summary: Signature requests now provide clearer delivery tracking, safer resend controls, and automatic follow-through for sequential signing.

highlights.title: Send the actionable request
highlights.description: Internal signature requests email the signer who can act next and retain delivery status for staff.

highlights.title: Track and resend safely
highlights.description: Staff can see delivery and first-view status and manually resend when follow-up is needed.

highlights.title: Keep sequential signing moving
highlights.description: Completing one signer notifies the next, while configured reminders run before expiration.

releases.title: Conflict reviews and portal invoice PDFs are traceable
releases.summary: Staff can save and close a conflict review, and clients can download a firm-branded invoice PDF from their matter portal.

highlights.title: Conflict searches keep their evidence
highlights.description: The new Conflict Search workspace saves the terms and results the reviewer saw, records notes and a decision, and locks the record after closing.

highlights.title: Restricted matters stay restricted
highlights.description: A reviewer is warned when a potential match exists on a matter they cannot access without exposing that matter's identity.

highlights.title: Clients can download branded invoices
highlights.description: A client-visible invoice is rendered with firm branding and streamed as a PDF; LawHand records download metadata and a hash without retaining another PDF copy.

releases.title: Prepare document templates with a guided review workspace
releases.summary: Turn PDFs and supported images into reusable document templates while reviewing every detected field before creation.

highlights.title: Review the original form in place
highlights.description: Prepare Form keeps the uploaded page design visible while you inspect, add, move, rename, and configure fields.

highlights.title: Recover fields from scans and images
highlights.description: Bounded local OCR and optional configured assistance can suggest fields without making automatic detection a requirement.

highlights.title: Finish safely when detection is imperfect
highlights.description: Validation, confidence cues, and manual placement let you correct unfamiliar forms before creating the reusable template.

releases.title: Customer cloud storage is explicit and fail-closed
releases.summary: Microsoft 365 tenants now default matter files to OneDrive, and portal uploads keep their original copy in a dedicated customer-cloud folder.

highlights.title: Microsoft 365 defaults to OneDrive
highlights.description: When Cloud Document Storage is Auto, an active Microsoft 365 connection is the authoritative destination unless an administrator selects SharePoint or Google Drive.

highlights.title: Portal originals have a stable home
highlights.description: Client uploads go to the matter's client_uploads folder. A reviewed or revised output is saved as a new matter document instead of silently moving the original.

highlights.title: Cloud outages fail honestly
highlights.description: A cloud-bound upload reports a retryable storage error when the customer provider is unavailable; it does not report success after saving a durable local copy.

releases.title: Tagged matter email can create traceable tasks
releases.summary: A reviewed matter email whose subject begins with [TASK] or [DEADLINE] can now be filed and turned into a linked task in one step.

highlights.title: Use an explicit subject tag
highlights.description: Start a new subject with [TASK] or [DEADLINE]. The tag must be the first token, so replies and forwarded subjects do not trigger.

highlights.title: Review the task before filing
highlights.description: The Correspondence queue previews the task title and any safely parsed due date before the reviewer chooses File + create task.

highlights.title: Keep the source email attached
highlights.description: The filed email, correspondence record, task, and task history remain linked so the source and resulting work can be audited from the matter.

releases.title: Demo workspaces reopen with approved matter-aware AI
releases.summary: Return to an active demo without a password, and demonstrate matter-aware Standard AI when Platform has approved the route.

highlights.title: Reopen an active demo
highlights.description: Choose Resume demo and enter the same email plus the current demo access code; the original expiry and AI quota stay unchanged.

highlights.title: Show matters with approved Standard AI
highlights.description: Standard can use matter and attachment context when its assigned Platform routing profile explicitly allows confidential context.

highlights.title: Control the demo route from Platform
highlights.description: Platform can choose the approved Standard profile assigned to new demos while Premium remains unavailable for disposable tenants.

releases.title: Guides now cover matter email and connected assistants
releases.summary: The in-product guides explain how matter email reaches a file and how to review or revoke an external assistant connected to your workspace.

highlights.title: Matter email is documented end to end
highlights.description: The user guide covers the Correspondence tab: capture rules and Scan now, forwarding addresses for a matter, and the queue where you file or reject a message.

highlights.title: Connected assistants are yours to review
highlights.description: The guide explains the Workspace MCP list in your profile ΓÇö what each connection holds, when it was last used, and how revoking one takes effect immediately.

highlights.title: Administrators can see who may connect
highlights.description: The administrative guide covers the per-user Workspace MCP control, the default for new accounts, and how consent-based access differs from a scoped product key.

releases.title: Workspace MCP connections respect your firmΓÇÖs access settings
releases.summary: Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, and other compatible assistants can connect when your firm administrator enables Workspace MCP for your account and Privacy Mode is off.

highlights.title: Firm access settings take effect directly
highlights.description: Admin ΓåÆ Users now separates firm permission, effective availability, and active OAuth connections, with a drawer to review or revoke each client.

highlights.title: Your privacy choice remains independent
highlights.description: Privacy Mode continues to pause external assistants, and turning it off allows a new explicit OAuth connection when firm access is enabled.

highlights.title: Security boundaries remain enforced
highlights.description: Active account, license, consent scope, role capability, token revocation, and tenant isolation checks still apply to every request.

releases.title: Research answers show and link the sources they use
releases.summary: Standard research now gives public authority to the assistant, mixed citations remain clickable, and the review-tag guide stays visible while an answer is prepared.

highlights.title: Standard answers can use retrieved public authority
highlights.description: Standard answers can now use retrieved public cases, statutes, and rules with review tags. Matter and firm information remain excluded from Standard.

highlights.title: Every retained source marker stays clickable
highlights.description: Answers that mix structured citation annotations with ordinary source markers now link both kinds to the authority or the in-answer source ledger.

highlights.title: Review tags and research progress stay in view
highlights.description: The tag legend remains visible on phones and desktops, and retrieved-source previews and elapsed research phases remain visible while Premium prepares a validated answer.

releases.title: Matter forwarding addresses can be created
releases.summary: Creating a secure forwarding address from a matter now completes normally instead of failing when the matter has no partner attorney.

highlights.title: Create the address from Correspondence
highlights.description: The Create address action now locks only the matter being updated, so the unique forwarding address appears immediately and is ready to use.

releases.title: Task details stay readable on phones
releases.summary: Mobile task rows now give the task name, due date, status, and actions their own space instead of squeezing them into one overlapping line.

highlights.title: Task names keep their space
highlights.description: The task name and notes use the full mobile row width, so longer names remain readable beside the completion checkbox.

highlights.title: Dates and actions wrap cleanly
highlights.description: Due dates, priority and unread badges, and task actions move onto a separate wrapping row instead of colliding or spilling off the screen.

releases.title: Forward email straight to the right matter
releases.summary: Give each matter its own secure forwarding address, see exactly which contact addresses are tracked, and review incoming mail before it becomes official correspondence.

highlights.title: Use one unique forwarding address per matter
highlights.description: Create an opaque address from the Correspondence tab and forward or BCC a message there without putting a client name or matter number in the address.

highlights.title: Review mail before filing it
highlights.description: Forwarded messages wait in a review queue until a firm user files or rejects them, so an email cannot silently become part of the matter record.

highlights.title: See what automatic matching tracks
highlights.description: Correspondence rules now list the client and matter-party email addresses they use instead of leaving the matching behavior implicit.

highlights.title: Rotate or disable an address immediately
highlights.description: Replace a forwarding address when it has been shared too broadly, or turn it off when the matter no longer needs inbound mail.

releases.title: A client portal that shows clients what needs their attention
releases.summary: The client portal now opens on what is waiting for the client, tracks what they have read, lets them sign out, and shows the firm whether an invitation is actually being used.

highlights.title: Clients see what needs them, first
highlights.description: The portal opens on unread messages, documents awaiting signature, shared documents, and the balance due, with the next key date called out and how soon it falls.

highlights.title: New messages are marked as new
highlights.description: Messages from the legal team show as unread and are counted on the tab until the client opens the thread, which refreshes on its own while they are reading it.

highlights.title: The legal team hears about a client message
highlights.description: When a client writes in through the portal, the people assigned to the matter are emailed a short preview and a link, rather than waiting for someone to notice.

highlights.title: Clients can sign out
highlights.description: A sign-out button ends the portal session immediately, so a borrowed or shared device does not keep access to the matter.

highlights.title: Invoices show what is actually owed
highlights.description: Each invoice shows the amount paid, the balance remaining, and how far past due it is, with a running total for the matter.

highlights.title: See whether a portal invitation was ever opened
highlights.description: The matter's Client Portal tab shows each invitation as awaiting first sign-in, active, expired, or revoked, and when it was last used.

releases.title: Network file shares, connected with their own credentials
releases.summary: Point LawHand at a file share that stays on your network: install the agent from a packaged installer, store the share's credentials securely, and test the connection before anyone searches it.

highlights.title: Install the file share agent instead of building it
highlights.description: Windows installs from an MSI that registers a background service and can pair during setup; Linux ships a binary with a service installer.

highlights.title: Store share credentials securely, per firm
highlights.description: Save the username and password, Kerberos, or guest identity each share needs. Secrets are encrypted, never shown again, and only reach your own agent.

highlights.title: Different shares can use different accounts
highlights.description: One agent can serve shares that need separate identities, and a credential can be restricted so it only ever reaches one agent.

highlights.title: Test a share before trusting it
highlights.description: Test connection asks the agent to mount the share and reports which identity it used, or the exact reason it failed, instead of leaving an empty index.

highlights.title: See when a share last indexed and why it stopped
highlights.description: Each share now shows its last scan time, file count, and failure reason, and can be rescanned on demand rather than waiting for its schedule.

releases.title: Teams calls land in your intake feed
releases.summary: Inbound Microsoft Teams Phone calls now appear in the intake dashboard beside Zoom Phone calls, and the Teams admin panel gains notification routing and a guided voice setup.

highlights.title: Teams Phone calls reach intake automatically
highlights.description: Inbound calls to your firm's Teams numbers appear in the intake dashboard beside Zoom Phone calls, with the same follow-up tasks and export.

highlights.title: Choose where each Teams notification lands
highlights.description: The Teams admin panel now routes each kind of notification to a team and channel you pick, with a matter's own linked channel still taking precedence.

highlights.title: Linked channels name the matter
highlights.description: The list of linked channels now shows the matter name instead of an internal identifier, so you can tell at a glance what each channel is bound to.

highlights.title: Teams errors say what to do
highlights.description: When Microsoft refuses a request, the panel explains what happened and how to fix it instead of showing an empty list of teams.

releases.title: Billing problems you can actually see
releases.summary: Your firm is now told when a subscription payment fails, slow pages say so instead of spinning, and Privacy Mode explains what it turns off.

highlights.title: Know about a payment problem before it costs you access
highlights.description: A banner now appears for everyone in the firm when a subscription payment fails or is suspended, with a direct route to update the payment method.

highlights.title: No more being offered a plan you already pay for
highlights.description: If the plan on file disagrees with the subscription your firm actually holds, the billing page says so and stops prompting you to buy again.

highlights.title: Slow is now distinguishable from stuck
highlights.description: Requests that take too long end with a clear message and a retry instead of an open-ended spinner, and long lists show their shape while loading.

highlights.title: Privacy Mode says what it affects
highlights.description: The Privacy Mode switch now states that it also blocks connected assistants, and the connected assistants list shows when access is blocked and why.

releases.title: A dedicated home for client relationships
releases.summary: Manage client details, communication preferences, matters, billing choices, and accounting connections from one secure workspace.

highlights.title: Keep the complete client profile together
highlights.description: Store contact details, addresses, emergency contacts, preferences, consent, internal notes, and relationship status in Clients & CRM.

highlights.title: See client work in context
highlights.description: Open a client to review linked matters, activity, tasks, and billing preferences without searching across separate screens.

highlights.title: Move client data safely
highlights.description: Tenant admins can import or export bounded CSV files and synchronize customer records with connected QuickBooks Online accounts.

releases.title: A clearer view of what changed
releases.summary: See the version currently running and catch up on the latest LawHand improvements without leaving your workspace.

highlights.title: Find updates in LawHand
highlights.description: Open Profile or Admin Settings to see the running version and the latest release notes.

highlights.title: Revise documents without losing the original
highlights.description: Each matter-document revision keeps the source document and its review history.

highlights.title: See where work stands
highlights.description: Move tasks through To Do, In Progress, Waiting, Review, and Done with clearer ownership and history.

highlights.title: Keep AI work available during provider limits
highlights.description: Premium requests can continue through the Standard route when premium capacity is temporarily unavailable.
